articles.title: Stimuli-responsive CRISPR-based genome editing delivery system for cancer treatment: A review of fundamentals and applications.
articles.abstract: Cancer remains a leading cause of mortality worldwide. Conventional modalities, namely surgery, radiotherapy, chemotherapy, and immunotherapy, continue to face substantial limitations. The advent of gene therapy, particularly CRISPR-based genome editing, offers new opportunities to overcome these barriers. Nuclease systems such as CRISPR/Cas9 enable precise excision of mutant alleles and targeted insertion of exogenous sequences by harnessing endogenous DNA-repair pathways, achieving durable and accurate genomic modification; derivative tools including CRISPRi, base editing, and prime editing enable diverse forms of gene regulation or precise genome modification through transcriptional repression, base conversion, or related editing mechanisms. To enhance the efficiency, specificity, and spatiotemporal control of CRISPR editing in vivo, sophisticated delivery platforms have been engineered to respond to endogenous tumor-microenvironment cues (e.g., pH, redox potential, hypoxia, ATP, enzymes and microRNAs) or exogenous triggers (e.g., light, ultrasound and magnetic fields). Distinct from material-centric classification schemes, this review organizes these stimuli-responsive systems according to their pathological relevance to the tumor microenvironment (TME), establishing a conceptual framework that links specific TME aberrations with corresponding delivery paradigms. These stimuli-responsive systems represent a major innovation and markedly expand the therapeutic potential of genome editing in oncology. In this review, we summarize the mechanistic basis of CRISPR-based editing, delineate design principles and engineering strategies for stimuli-responsive delivery, and highlight recent advances, outstanding challenges, and future directions toward clinical translation. We aim to provide a concise reference to guide the rational design of gene-editing cancer therapeutics.

articles.title: Advancing Precision Therapeutics in Older Adults: A Scoping Review of Pharmacogenomic Service Models.
articles.abstract: Older adults remain a therapeutically understudied population despite experiencing the highest burden of polypharmacy, age-related pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic variability, and medication-related harm. Pharmacogenomic testing offers an opportunity to individualize drug therapy in this population; however, its clinical implementation is complicated by population-specific challenges. We conducted a scoping review to describe existing pharmacogenomic testing services implemented in adults aged ≥ 65 years and to identify design features that support translation of genomic information into therapeutic decision making. Five databases were searched from inception to May 2026. Studies were included if pharmacogenomic test results were used to inform prescribing decisions. Data were extracted on pre-implementation actions, implementation workflows and types of outcomes assessed. The review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines. Eleven pharmacogenomic services were identified, implemented across diverse settings including primary care, geriatric clinics, residential aged care, pharmacies, and telepharmacies. Multiple design elements were deduced to support therapeutic integration of pharmacogenomic testing: (1) leveraging medication management workflows, (2) delivering pre-implementation healthcare professional education, (3) targeting population-relevant gene and allele panels, (4) establishing simplified organizational guidelines, (5) utilizing clinical decision support tools to identify drug-gene and drug-drug-gene interactions, (6) pharmacist-led interpretation of results, and (7) iterative service evaluation. Notably, most services were embedded within broader medication management programs, positioning pharmacogenomic testing as a tool to refine, rather than replace, existing therapeutic decision making in older adults. The findings provide a pragmatic framework for designing pharmacogenomic services that advance precision therapeutics in older adults and highlight priorities for future implementation and evaluation.

articles.title: Conditional biologics in cancer immunotherapy: mechanisms, applications and clinical progress.
articles.abstract: Immunotherapy has transformed cancer treatment, enabling durable responses and long-term survival in many patients. However, widespread use remains limited by refractory indications, immune-related toxicities and acquired resistance. Complications such as cytokine release syndrome, immune-related adverse events, infusion-related reactions and on-target, off-tumour toxicities have emerged as specific safety concerns. Approaches that can direct immunotherapy to the tumour microenvironment (TME), such as intratumoural administration, have only partially mitigated these risks and present additional logistical and technical barriers. Conditional biologics, in which proteins are engineered to become active in response to tumour-associated signals or in the TME, enable the uncoupling of efficacy from toxicity. By enhancing tumour accumulation, targeting activity to a particular cell type and minimizing off-target effects, conditional activation offers a potential strategy to expand the therapeutic window of cancer therapeutics. This Review provides a comprehensive overview of the mechanisms, applications, challenges and future directions of this approach, while assessing completed and ongoing clinical trials.

articles.title: Histone lysine demethylases in the third decade: biology and therapeutic prospects.
articles.abstract: Histone post-translational modifications, such as methylation, acetylation, phosphorylation and ubiquitination, have fundamental roles in regulating chromatin structure and gene expression. Histone methylation was once considered a static modification until the discovery of the histone lysine demethylase LSD1 (KDM1A), more than two decades ago. Since then, numerous KDMs in two main enzyme classes have been identified. Their diverse roles in regulating gene expression, metabolism, immune responses and disease pathogenesis have been extensively studied and small-molecule inhibitors have been developed. KDMs exert context-dependent functions as either oncogenes or tumour suppressors, which complicates their therapeutic targeting. As we enter the third decade of investigations into histone demethylation, unlocking the full therapeutic potential of inhibiting KDMs will require a deeper understanding of their biology, substrate specificity, interaction networks and regulatory crosstalk. In this Review, we discuss the functions of KDMs in metabolic and immune regulation and their roles in cancer and other diseases. We describe the landscape of KDM inhibitors, especially LSD1 inhibitors, which are the most advanced demethylase inhibitors in clinical trials. We highlight the need for more potent and selective KDM inhibitors, biomarkers of therapeutic response, novel combinatorial treatments and innovative drug discovery strategies.

articles.title: Confirmed Multiple Drug Hypersensitivity Syndrome is Uncommon, and its Culprit Drug Spectrum Reflects Patterns of Drug Exposure.
articles.abstract: Multiple drug hypersensitivity syndrome (MDHS) is defined as confirmed hypersensitivity to two or more chemically and pharmacologically unrelated drug entities. Few studies have characterized MDHS with systematic diagnostic confirmation. We aimed to determine the frequency, culprit drug patterns, and diagnostic findings of confirmed MDHS. We retrospectively reviewed patients evaluated for suspected drug hypersensitivity at a Korean tertiary allergy center from March 2017 to April 2026. MDHS required confirmed hypersensitivity to at least two unrelated drug entities by skin testing, serum-specific IgE, or provocation testing; cross-reactive reactions were not counted separately. Among 6684 evaluated patients, 3007 underwent diagnostic testing, and 1380 were tested for multiple suspected drugs. MDHS was confirmed in 94 patients (1.4%, 3.1%, and 6.8%, respectively). Anaphylaxis was the most common manifestation (38.3%). Most patients (84.0%) reacted to two entities, whereas 12.8% and 3.2% reacted to three and four entities, respectively. Leading culprits were β-lactams (n = 34), nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs)/acetaminophen (n = 34), antituberculosis agents (n = 27), and histamine-2 receptor antagonists (n = 19). Recurrent combinations involved first-line antituberculosis agents and NSAIDs plus ranitidine. Of 114 entities confirmed by drug provocation, 38 had negative preceding skin tests. Delayed-reading intradermal testing was more frequently positive in drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS) than in maculopapular exanthema (MPE) (53.3% vs. 0.0%, P = 0.008). Confirmed MDHS was uncommon despite suspected hypersensitivity to multiple drugs. The clinical presentation resembled European cohorts, whereas the culprit spectrum reflected regional prescribing patterns. Systematically evaluating each suspected entity may preserve future treatment options.

articles.title: Green Tea Extract Decreases the Systemic Exposure of Pazopanib in Healthy Participants.
articles.abstract: Green tea catechins modulate the activity of key drug pharmacokinetic determinants and consequently, concomitant consumption of green tea can significantly alter systemic drug exposure. This study aimed to investigate the influence of concomitant green tea catechin consumption on the pharmacokinetics of pazopanib, a tyrosine kinase inhibitor used in the treatment of advanced renal cell carcinoma and advanced soft tissue sarcoma. An open-label, single-dose, fixed-sequence pharmacokinetic study in 15 healthy participants was conducted. Participants were administered a 200 mg pazopanib tablet on Day 1 (Control Period) and Day 15, and an 833 mg green tea extract tablet once daily on Days 10-18 (Green Tea Extract Period). Fourteen healthy participants completed the study. Concomitant green tea extract consumption significantly reduced pazopanib oral systemic exposure. The geometric mean ratios (Green Tea Extract/Control) for pazopanib maximum plasma concentration (Cmax), area under the plasma concentration-time curve (AUC) from time 0 to last quantifiable timepoint (AUC0-t), AUC extrapolated to infinity (AUC0-∞) and half-life (t1/2) were 0.44 (90% CI: 0.30-0.64, n = 14), 0.53 (90% CI: 0.41-0.68, n = 13), 0.57 (90% CI: 0.44-0.74, n = 13) and 1.12 (90% CI: 1.05-1.20, n = 13), respectively. Median pazopanib time of Cmax (Tmax) was slightly shorter in the Control Period (4.0 h) than the Green Tea Extract Period (4.5 h, P < 0.01, n = 14). Given the established concentration-response relationships for pazopanib anticancer effects, decreases in pazopanib systemic exposure with green tea catechin consumption may be clinically important.

articles.title: 18F-Florquinitau PET for imaging tau pathology in Alzheimer's disease.
Bioorthogonal sticky-PROTACs for targeted and sustained protein degradation.
articles.abstract: Proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) can catalytically eliminate disease-driving proteins, but nonspecific exposure, rapid clearance, and concentration-dependent hook effects limit their tumor selectivity and durability. Here, we report a kinetically programmed bioorthogonal sticky PROTAC (VPT) that temporally separates tumor capture from prodrug activation. Tetrazine (Tz) handles were selectively installed on HER2-overexpressing tumor cells through antibody-directed metabolic glycoengineering. VPT integrates a trans-cyclooctene (TCO) group for rapid Tz-mediated covalent anchoring with a vinyl ether (VE) cage for slower Tz-triggered release of an active BRD4 degrader. The TCO-Tz ligation proceeded approximately 4890-fold faster than VE-Tz cleavage, enabling rapid tumor-cell retention followed by sustained local activation. In HER2-pretargeted cells, VPT prolonged BRD4 degradation after washout, showed no evident hook effect within the tested concentration range. Bioorthogonal anchoring also maintained tumor-associated fluorescence for up to 120 h. In SKOV3 and BT474 xenografts, HER2-MTz plus VPT achieved tumor growth inhibition rates of 85.8% and 95.7%, respectively, outperforming the corresponding non-sticky control. This dual-kinetics design provides a generalizable strategy for coupling tumor-selective retention with sustained in situ PROTAC activation.

articles.title: Selective ORgan-targeting lipid nanoparticles deliver SMAD7 mRNA to fibrotic lungs and attenuate pulmonary fibrosis.
articles.abstract: Fibroblast activation and differentiation into myofibroblasts drive excessive extracellular matrix deposition and irreversible scarring in pulmonary fibrosis, such as idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), underscoring the need for therapies that directly target fibroblast activation. Here, we apply engineered lung-targeting Selective ORgan-Targeting (SORT) lipid nanoparticles for intravenous RNA delivery to fibrotic lungs. In a preclinical model of pulmonary fibrosis, engineered SORT LNPs achieved functional mRNA delivery in approximately 20% of CD45-CD31-EpCAM-Thy1.2+ mesenchymal cells in fibrotic lungs. Mechanistic studies further supported a contributory role of the vitronectin (Vtn)/vitronectin receptor (VtnR) axis in 1A7B13 Lung SORT LNP uptake. Therapeutic delivery of SMAD7 mRNA inhibited fibroblast activation in human lung fibroblast cultures and attenuated pulmonary fibrosis in vivo, resulting in an approximately 40% reduction in histological collagen deposition and a significant reduction in lung hydroxyproline content. Together, these findings establish engineered lung-enriched SORT LNPs as a platform for systemic RNA delivery to fibrotic lungs, including disease-relevant mesenchymal populations, and demonstrate their potential for RNA-based anti-fibrotic therapy.

articles.title: Caffeic acid regulates the gut microbiota-tryptophan metabolic axis to improve intestinal barrier function and relieve ulcerative colitis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic inflammatory bowel disease for which current therapies remain inadequate. Caffeic acid (CA), a natural hydroxycinnamic acid polyphenol, possesses anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties. However, whether CA engages the gut microbiota-tryptophan-aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AHR)-Nrf2 axis in UC has not been established. PURPOSE: To evaluate the anti-UC activity of CA in vivo and in vitro and to elucidate its underlying mechanisms through a multi-platform integrative strategy. STUDY DESIGN: A dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced murine colitis model and lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated mouse colonic epithelial cells (MCECs) were used in parallel. Mechanism was addressed by combining microbiota, metabolomic, transcriptomic and proteomic profiling with faecal microbiota transplantation, computational and biophysical target validation, and siRNA-mediated AHR knockdown. METHODS: CA was administered at 10 and 20 mg/kg/day, with 5-aminosalicylic acid as positive control. Complementary platforms included 16S rRNA gut microbiota sequencing, untargeted serum metabolomics, colonic transcriptomic profiling, data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry proteomics, human UC single-cell RNA sequencing (GEO: GSE214695), faecal microbiota transplantation into antibiotic-pretreated recipients, molecular docking, 100 ns molecular dynamics simulation, cellular thermal shift assay, dual-luciferase reporter assay, and co-immunoprecipitation. RESULTS: CA dose-dependently alleviated dextran sulfate sodium-induced colitis, suppressed NF-κB activation, and reduced interleukin-6, interleukin-1β, and tumour necrosis factor alpha. Gut microbiota profiling revealed enrichment of Bifidobacterium and Dubosiella with depletion of Escherichia-Shigella. Transplantation of the CA-remodelled microbiota into antibiotic-pretreated recipients reproduced the protective phenotype and restored colonic AHR and cytochrome P450 1A1 expression, demonstrating that the remodelled community is sufficient to confer protection. Metabolomics showed enrichment of serotonin-branch tryptophan metabolites, with 5-hydroxytryptamine among the most significantly enriched differential metabolites. Molecular docking and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulation indicated stable binding of CA within the AHR ligand-binding domain, cellular thermal shift assay confirmed intracellular target engagement, and a dual-luciferase reporter assay demonstrated concentration-dependent activation of dioxin response element-driven transcription, establishing CA as an AHR agonist. CA increased Nrf2, NQO1 and HO-1 and restored Claudin-1, Occludin and zonula occludens-1; AHR knockdown reduced these effects and the suppression of NF-κB, indicating that both actions depend on AHR. CONCLUSIONS: CA ameliorates UC through convergent AHR activation, arising from both microbiota-mediated tryptophan reprogramming and direct receptor binding, with AHR-dependent Nrf2/NQO1/HO-1 induction and NF-κB suppression to restore intestinal barrier integrity. These findings support CA as a multi-target phytochemical candidate for UC treatment.

articles.title: Iberdomide: First Approval.
articles.abstract: Iberdomide (ZENBEXUS™) is a cereblon E3 ligase modulator being developed by Bristol Myers Squibb and its subsidiary Celgene Corporation for the treatment of various haematological malignancies, including multiple myeloma. On 13 August 2026, iberdomide received accelerated approval in the USA for use in combination with daratumumab and hyaluronidase-fihj and dexamethasone for the treatment of adult patients with multiple myeloma who have received at least one prior line of therapy including a proteasome inhibitor and an immunomodulatory agent. On 30 September 2026, iberdomide received conditional approval in China for use in combination with daratumumab and dexamethasone to treat adult patients with multiple myeloma who have received at least one first-line therapy (including a proteasome inhibitor and an immunomodulatory agent). This article summarizes the milestones in the development of iberdomide leading to this first approval for multiple myeloma.

articles.title: Enlicitide: First Approval.
articles.abstract: Enlicitide (LIPFENDRA®) is a proprotein convertase subtilisin kexin type 9 (PCSK9) inhibitor being developed by Merck Sharp & Dohme for the treatment of dyslipidaemias. On 16 July 2026, enlicitide received its first approval in the USA where it is indicated as an adjunct to diet and exercise to reduce low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) in adults with hypercholesterolaemia, including heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia (HeFH). This article summarizes the milestones in the development of enlicitide leading to this first approval for hypercholesterolaemia.

articles.title: Ciguatoxins alter RyR2 gating, intracellular Ca²⁺ handling and cardiac function in human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes and rats.
articles.abstract: Ciguatoxins (CTXs) cause ciguatera, a seafood-borne intoxication frequently associated with cardiovascular manifestations, but the underlying cardiac mechanisms remain poorly understood. We investigated the effects of purified CTX-1B and CTX-3 C in human induced pluripotent stem-cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hiPSC-CMs), porcine cardiac ryanodine receptor type 2 (RyR2) channels, and rats. In hiPSC-CMs, CTX-1B and CTX-3 C (0.3-5 nM) rapidly increased diastolic intracellular Ca²⁺ and altered spontaneous Ca²⁺ transients. At 5 nM, CTXs increased transient frequency, reduced transient amplitude, impaired contractile performance, and disrupted sarcomeric organisation. In planar lipid bilayers, CTX-1B (1 nM) prolonged RyR2 openings under resting cytosolic Ca²⁺ conditions and remodelled channel gating after activation with ATP (25 µM). Molecular docking predicted a CTX-1B interaction region within the RyR2 transmembrane domain, close to ligand-sensitive regulatory elements, supporting state-dependent modulation of channel gating. Cardiac sheets exposed to CTX showed reduced spontaneous field-potential activity and contraction. In rats, intravenous CTX-1B administration (0.13 ng/g bodyweight) caused bradycardia, premature atrial and ventricular contractions, atrioventricular conduction abnormalities, and atrial flutter. Echocardiography revealed impaired myocardial deformation and relaxation despite preserved ejection fraction. These findings identify altered RyR2 gating and intracellular Ca²⁺ dysregulation as plausible complementary contributors to CTX cardiotoxicity and extend the established mechanism based on persistent voltage-gated Na⁺-channel activation. Combined disruption of sarcolemmal excitability and intracellular Ca²⁺ release could explain the acute electrical and mechanical cardiac abnormalities associated with ciguatera.

articles.title: Natural products mitigate pyrethroid-induced male reproductive toxicity: a systematic review.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pyrethroids are among the most widely used pesticides worldwide and cause reproductive toxicity through oxidative stress, endocrine disruption, and testicular damage. Numerous studies have explored antioxidant-rich natural products and other bioactive compounds to mitigate the effects of pyrethroid exposure. PURPOSE: This systematic review comprehensively evaluates the evidence on the efficacy of natural products in mitigating pyrethroid-induced reproductive toxicity in experimental models. METHODS: Following PRISMA guidelines, PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase were searched from database inception to July 2025. The animal experimental studies evaluating natural products against pyrethroid-induced reproductive toxicity in adult male laboratory animals were included. Outcomes included sperm parameters, hormonal balance, oxidative stress markers, and testicular histopathology. Study quality and risk of bias were assessed using the ARRIVE guidelines and SYRCLE's Risk of Bias tool for animal studies, respectively. RESULTS AND DISCUSSION: Thirty-three animal experimental studies were included in this review. Most indicate that pyrethroid exposure consistently decreased sperm count, motility, and testosterone levels, increased oxidative stress, and disrupted the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal (HPG) axis. The studies show that natural products such as sage (Salvia officinalis), rosemary (Salvia rosmarinus), onion (Allium cepa), ginseng (Panax ginseng), curcumin, quercetin, and resveratrol may ameliorate these effects. CONCLUSION: Proposed mechanisms of natural products include enhanced antioxidant defenses, hormonal regulation, DNA protection, and preservation of testicular, structure although direct evidence for these pathways remains limited and has largely been inferred from a subset of the included studies rather than established as generalizable mechanisms. Nanoparticle formulations may improve bioavailability and efficacy. Natural antioxidants show promise in reducing pyrethroid-induced reproductive toxicity in male experimental animals. Further standardized research and clinical trials are essential to establish translational potential. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD42022348260.

articles.title: Botanical interventions for alcohol hangover: a scoping review.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Botanical interventions are widely studied and marketed for alcohol hangover, but direct symptom evidence, biomarker findings, and preclinical results are frequently conflated. This scoping review mapped the clinical and preclinical evidence for botanical interventions for alcohol hangover and examined the reproducibility of botanical and extract reporting. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, CBM, CNKI, VIP, and Wanfang Data were searched from inception to 22 July 2025. Citation searching and peer-reviewer recommendation were used as additional identification methods. Evidence was organized as Level 1 (direct human hangover symptoms), Level 2 (human pharmacokinetic/exposure, biochemical, mechanistic, and pharmacogenetic outcomes), and Level 3 (preclinical animal evidence); safety was charted separately. Botanical identity and extract characterization were charted using a ConPhyMP-informed framework. RESULTS: Twenty-two studies reported in 21 publications were included: 15 human studies and seven animal studies, with one publication containing both human and animal experiments. Across the human studies, 470 participants were enrolled or randomized and 437 were included in the reported analyses. Sex was available for 400 analyzed participants, of whom 293 (73.3%) were male. Direct symptom evidence was heterogeneous: seven publications showed a positive signal, six were mixed, and two were null. Pharmacokinetic or biomarker changes were not treated as substitutes for symptom improvement. Scientific botanical identity was reported in 19/21 publications, whereas authentication and voucher numbers were reported in only 3/21 each; quantitative marker analysis or a defined phytochemical profile was reported in 8/21. Safety reporting was inconsistent. CONCLUSION: Several botanical interventions showed preliminary signals in selected hangover symptoms or alcohol-related biomarkers, but the clinical evidence remains limited and heterogeneous and includes mixed and null findings. The current evidence is insufficient to establish routine therapeutic efficacy or long-term safety. Future studies should prioritize adequately powered trials with validated symptom outcomes, clear prevention-versus-treatment timing, and reproducible botanical and phytochemical characterization. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://osf.io/cv83d, identifier https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/CV83D.

articles.title: PC6 injection enhanced the preventive effect against postoperative nausea of granisetron compared with intravenous injection in gynecological laparoscopic patients: a randomized controlled study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Moderate to severe postoperative nausea and vomiting significantly impedes recovery and is inadequately managed by current pharmacotherapy. This study investigates whether granisetron injection at the PC6 acupoint enhances prevention of postoperative moderate to severe postoperative nausea and vomiting compared to intravenous injection. METHODS: 244 participants undergoing elective gynecologic endoscopic surgery under general anesthesia were randomly assigned to PC6 granisetron group, IV granisetron group, PC6 saline group and control group. All patients receive 5 mg dexamethasone during anesthesia induction. At the end of surgery, 2 mg granisetron was injected at the PC6 acupoint in PC6 granisetron group, 2 mg granisetron was injected intravenously in IV granisetron group, 2 ml saline was injected at the PC6 acupoint in PC6 saline group, no additional measures to prevent postoperative nausea and vomiting in control group. RESULTS: The incidence of moderate-to-severe postoperative nausea in PC6 granisetron group was significantly lower than that in IV granisetron group, PC6 saline group and control group within 24 h after surgery. (14.8% [9/61] vs. 32.8% [20/61]; RR = 0.45, [95% CI: 0.22, 0.91]; P = 0.02 (14.8% [9/61] vs. 29.5% [18/61]; RR = 0.50 [95% CI: 0.24, 1.02]; P = 0.058, (14.8% [9/61] vs. 43.9% [25/57]; RR = 0.34 [95% CI: 0.17, 0.66]; P < 0.01.) These differences started from 2 h after surgery. There was no adverse events about PC6 acupoint injection was found. CONCLUSION: Granisetron injection at the PC6 acupoint enhances prevention of moderate-to-severe postoperative nausea within 24 h after surgery in patients undergoing elective gynecologic laparoscopic surgery under general anesthesia. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was registered at http://www.chictr.org.cn (ChiCTR2400085300).

articles.title: Strategies for overcoming extracellular and intracellular delivery barriers in Liver-Targeted gene therapy.
articles.abstract: Liver-targeted gene therapy holds great potential for treating diverse hepatic disorders, yet its efficacy is significantly hindered by complex extracellular and intracellular delivery barriers. This review systematically delineates the pathophysiological obstacles that impede the efficient delivery of nucleic acid drugs, spanning from systemic clearance and tissue penetration to cellular uptake and intracellular trafficking. A particular focus is placed on recent advances in engineered non-viral delivery systems designed to prolong systemic circulation and achieve disease-relevant cell-specific targeting, as well as innovative methods to enhance tissue permeation, facilitate cell membrane crossing, and ensure efficient endosomal escape with subsequent subcellular localization. Furthermore, the therapeutic application of these platforms for both monogenic and complex liver diseases is critically evaluated, with attention to their potential and persistent bottlenecks in clinical applications. Integrating insights into barrier biology with rational nanomaterial design would facilitate the development of next‑generation non‑viral gene therapies for precise and effective treatment of hepatic disorders.

articles.title: Metformin for the treatment of chronic liver disease: Mechanistic rationale, translational evidence, and repurposing opportunities.
articles.abstract: Chronic liver disease (CLD) is characterized by progressive hepatocellular injury, metabolic dysfunction, inflammation, fibrogenesis, and an increased risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Despite advances in understanding CLD pathogenesis, effective therapies targeting multiple disease-driving pathways remain limited. Metformin, a biguanide widely used to treat type 2 diabetes, has emerged as a candidate for drug repurposing because of its pleiotropic metabolic and immunomodulatory effects. This narrative review examines the mechanistic rationale, translational evidence, and clinical implications of metformin in treating CLD. Experimental studies indicate that metformin modulates AMP-activated protein kinase-dependent and -independent pathways involved in hepatic lipid metabolism, mitochondrial bioenergetics, oxidative stress, autophagy, immunometabolic signaling, hepatic stellate cell activation, and hepatocarcinogenesis. In preclinical models, these effects have been associated with reduced steatosis, inflammatory injury, fibrogenesis, and tumor-promoting signaling. Epidemiological and clinical studies also suggest that metformin use is associated with improved survival in selected patients with cirrhosis and a lower risk of HCC in individuals with diabetes. Although mechanistic, experimental, and epidemiological evidence is encouraging, randomized clinical studies have not consistently shown histological improvement in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis, and clinical findings remain heterogeneous across disease stages and etiologies. Limitations include the gap between mechanistic and clinical evidence, uncertainty regarding the relevance of proposed mechanisms, the context-dependent nature of metformin signaling, and the inherent limitations of observational studies. Overall, metformin is a biologically plausible therapeutic candidate for CLD, but its future clinical role will depend on integrating mechanistic insights with rigorous translational and clinical research to identify patients most likely to benefit.

articles.title: Elucidating lysosomal dysfunction in cardiac fibrosis progression: Molecular understanding and pharmacological targeting strategies.
articles.abstract: Cardiac fibrosis is a critical pathological condition characterized by an excessive accumulation of extracellular matrix components resulting from persistent cellular stress, inflammation, oxidative stress, and organelle dysfunction. These insoluble fibers form a 3D matrix that is evident in numerous heart-related conditions, including myocardial infarction, heart failure, cardiomyopathies, and hypertension. Cardiomyocytes, unlike fibroblasts and endothelial cells, are post-mitotic and rely heavily on cellular quality-control systems to sustain their workload. Lysosomes, a single-lipid-bilayered membrane-bound organelle, are one of the important organelles that maintain cellular homeostasis by degrading and recycling cellular debris. Autophagy is one of the catabolic processes that is heavily reliant on lysosomes to form autolysosomes, which help degrade and recycle cellular components, proteins, and lipids, and maintain cellular homeostasis. Recently, lysosomal dysfunction has been found to play a critical contributing role in modulating cardiac fibrosis. The involvement of lysosomal dysfunction in mediating cardiac fibrosis progression involves several intriguing mechanisms that regulate lysosomal integrity, including V-ATPase, transcription factor EB (TFEB), lysosomal-associated membrane protein-2 (LAMP-2), cathepsin B, and chaperone-mediated autophagy, among others. The subsequent review, therefore, demonstrates the role of lysosomes in physiological and pathological heart conditions, with a particular emphasis on cardiac fibrosis, the central mechanism underlying the most aggressive stages of cardiac disease. The correlation between lysosomal dysfunction and cardiac fibrosis, as well as the interconnections and cellular pathways linking them, is discussed, along with emerging preclinical and clinical investigations that could be pursued to elucidate the role of lysosomal dysfunction in cardiac fibrosis progression.

articles.title: Beyond ACE2 downregulation: daphnetin as a multi-target agent for COVID-19 and rheumatic comorbidities.
articles.abstract: The continuous emergence of SARS-CoV-2 variants (e.g., JN.1, KP.3) and the significantly elevated risk of severe COVID-19 in patients with rheumatic autoimmune diseases highlight an urgent unmet clinical need for dual-targeted therapeutics. Daphnetin (7,8-dihydroxycoumarin), a natural coumarin compound with a long history of clinical use in China, prevents SARS-CoV-2 infection by downregulating the viral entry receptor ACE2 through inhibition of HIF-1α and JAK2/STAT3 signaling. This review synthesizes the pleiotropic pharmacological mechanisms of daphnetin, including anti-inflammatory (NF-κB, JAK/STAT, NLRP3), antioxidant (Nrf2/Keap1), immunomodulatory (Th17/Treg balance), and mitochondrial protective pathways. These pathways are critically involved in the pathogenesis of both severe COVID-19 and rheumatic diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). We propose that daphnetin represents a novel "one agent, dual protection" strategy: it not only blocks viral entry by reducing ACE2 but also mitigates the hyperinflammatory and oxidative stress states that exacerbate both COVID-19 severity and rheumatic disease activity. Given its established safety, oral activity, and low cost, daphnetin is a promising candidate for clinical translation in high-risk comorbid populations. Key unresolved questions and future research directions are also discussed.

articles.title: Traditional Chinese medicine interventions for hyperhomocysteinemia-associated vascular injury: an evidence-mapped, mitochondria-centered review.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Hyperhomocysteinemia (HHcy) is associated with vascular injury. Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) has an ethnopharmacological background in vascular disorders, and contemporary evidence warrants focused evaluation in HHcy-associated vascular injury. AIM OF THE STUDY: To integrate clinical and experimental TCM evidence, distinguish direct HHcy/Hcy evidence from supportive evidence, and map mechanistic relationships and evidence boundaries. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This structured narrative review with evidence mapping searched PubMed, Web of Science Core Collection, and CNKI Academic Journals through October 13, 2026, and classified evidence according to intervention identity and HHcy directness. Formal study-level risk-of-bias assessment was not completed for the final human evidence set. RESULTS: The review identified 71 scientifically distinct intervention-level entities: 9 extracts/fractions, 27 isolated compounds, 14 formulas/herb pairs, 16 patent/marketed medicines, 3 combination regimens, and 2 derivatives/salts. The final direct-evidence set comprised 199 independent direct studies, including 84 human, 45 animal, and 70 directly relevant experimental studies. Mechanistic findings were synthesized qualitatively across recurring vascular and mitochondrial themes; quantitative network topology was not reported because independently verified edge-level provenance was not established. CONCLUSIONS: TCM interventions show broad mechanistic evidence relevant to HHcy-associated vascular injury, but the qualitative evidence map reflects mechanistic coverage rather than therapeutic efficacy. Evidence remains predominantly experimental/preclinical, and evidence for durable cardiovascular or cerebrovascular benefit remains insufficient. Further work requires standardized interventions, rigorous mechanistic validation, and well-designed clinical studies assessing long-term safety and vascular outcomes.

articles.title: Nanomaterials for endometriosis: a multimodal strategy integrating targeted delivery, immunomodulation, and physical ablation.
articles.abstract: Endometriosis is a chronic inflammatory condition for which existing treatments, mainly hormonal therapy and surgical intervention, remain insufficient. These approaches are often limited by high recurrence rates, significant side effects, and an inability to effectively target underlying disease mechanisms. This review outlines emerging mechanism-oriented therapeutic strategies that combine targeted drug delivery, immunomodulation, and physical ablation. Advanced delivery systems, such as Lipid nanoparticle polymeric carriers, and nanomicelles, enable selective accumulation of therapeutic agents at endometriotic lesions, improving efficacy while minimizing systemic toxicity. Immunomodulatory strategies pursue to re-establish immune balance by enhancing immune surveillance, driving macrophage polarization toward anti-inflammatory states, and suppressing pro-inflammatory signaling, often through nanocarrier-enabled localized delivery. Furthermore, physical ablation techniques including gold (Au) NPs-mediated photothermal therapy and magnetic hyperthermia offer minimally invasive approaches for precise lesion elimination while preserving adjacent healthy tissues. Collectively, integrating these strategies may advance preclinical efforts to improve disease management, patient stratification, and potentially fertility outcomes, although clinical validation is still required. Despite ongoing challenges in clinical translation, the convergence of nanotechnology, immunology and interventional therapy marks a conceptual shift away from symptom-centered management toward investigational strategies that, pending clinical validation, may confer disease-modifying potential in endometriosis.

articles.title: Hepatocyte protection and stellate cell control by Salvia miltiorrhiza in liver fibrosis.
articles.abstract: Salvia miltiorrhiza Bunge provides chemically distinct candidates for hepatocyte protection and hepatic stellate cell (HSC) control. This critical narrative Mini Review examines whether these effects occur with one defined intervention at compatible exposure. HSC control is distinguished as elimination, sustained deactivation after withdrawal or short-term state suppression. Same-study observations include hepatocyte protection with HSC state suppression and salvianolic acid A-induced apoptosis in PDGF-stimulated HSCs with preserved primary-hepatocyte viability. These findings provide partial support for cellular selectivity, but do not establish injured-hepatocyte rescue and HSC control within a pharmacologically supported exposure interval. Opposing ferroptosis effects among tanshinones further preclude class-level mechanistic inference. Clinical findings concern specific preparations and endpoints, and do not resolve the paired cellular question. Priorities are chemical and batch characterization, authenticated human models, validated fate endpoints, state- or subset-selectivity that preserves HSC homeostatic functions, and measurement of achieved exposure and target engagement. A useful window should meet separate hepatocyte-benefit, safety and HSC-control criteria, with donor-level effect estimates and confidence intervals. Distinguishing intrinsic susceptibility from delivery-mediated enrichment is essential for translating these candidates into reproducible antifibrotic interventions.

articles.title: Dietary phytochemicals targeting neuroinflammation: mechanisms, bioavailability and translational challenges.
articles.abstract: Neuroinflammation and oxidative stress are among the most common and fundamental biochemical mechanisms underlying many neurological disorders, and both are promising therapeutic targets. Neuroinflammation and oxidative stress are bidirectional, and each could trigger and amplify the other. Since activated immune cells during neuroinflammation produce high levels of ROS, creating a vicious biochemical cycle, targeting neuroinflammation is an ideal opportunity to curtail both neuroinflammation and oxidative stress. The initiation and progression of neuroinflammation cause structural and functional damage to both neurons and glial cells in the central nervous system. Early intervention to inhibit neuroinflammation could prevent irreversible damage to the nervous tissue. The current application of glucocorticosteroids and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs in neurological disorders poses a risk of injury to the cardiovascular, gastrointestinal, respiratory, hepatic, and renal systems. Bioactive phytochemicals derived from dietary herbal medicines with demonstrated anti-inflammatory activity could serve as effective substitutes. Although very few of these phytochemicals have undergone clinical trials demonstrating efficacy and safety, several limitations, including lower bioavailability, solubility, and stability, hinder their clinical use. The purpose of this review is to identify preclinical data on multiple dietary bioactive phytochemicals with robust anti-neuroinflammatory effects that could be considered for clinical trials. Based on sufficient, efficacious, predominantly preclinical data, this review highlights the need for future modifications to enhance bioavailability while maintaining or improving therapeutic efficacy, with reduced systemic side effects, for these phytochemicals, rather than evaluating their potency in newer disease models or exploring new mechanisms. Further, prioritizing the identification of top-tier phytochemicals or their combinations that exhibit high bioavailability, optimal dosing, and proven long-term safety, while minimizing drug interactions and systemic toxicity through a standardized set of preclinical studies, is essential to manage chronic neuroinflammation with phytochemicals.

articles.title: Mitochondrial cristae remodeling in ischemic stroke: mechanisms and therapeutic perspectives.
articles.abstract: Mitochondrial cristae arrange the respiratory machinery within the inner membrane and change as ischemia gives way to reperfusion. Their organization depends on mitochondrial contact site and cristae organizing system assemblies, optic atrophy 1, adenosine triphosphate synthase, and cardiolipin. Disruption of these systems can impair energy production, facilitate neuronal death, and expose mitochondrial DNA to inflammatory sensors. This review brings structural work together with experimental stroke studies to examine how crista remodeling contributes to injury and recovery. Genetic manipulation of selected regulators has preserved mitochondrial structure and reduced injury in neurons and microglia. Most of these interventions preceded ischemia, leaving the speed and feasibility of repair after stroke onset uncertain. Pharmacological modulation and mitochondrial delivery offer ways to address this gap, particularly around reperfusion. Emerging strategies combine modulation of crista protein assemblies with cardiolipin directed treatment, mitochondrial antioxidant nanomedicine, organelle delivery, and control of local drug exposure. Their therapeutic evaluation can be aligned with distinct opportunities at reperfusion and during subsequent tissue recovery. Progress toward treatment will require evidence that a candidate reaches the affected brain cells, modifies the intended membrane assembly, and produces lasting neurological benefit. The available studies place crista remodeling within neuroprotective pathways and identify the experimental steps needed to evaluate it as a therapeutic target.

articles.title: Computational drug screening for drug-resistant tuberculosis: advances, challenges, and future perspectives.
articles.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB), caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, remains a major global health challenge, further exacerbated by the rapid emergence of drug-resistant strains. Despite continuous efforts, the discovery of novel anti-TB agents has lagged behind the evolution of resistance, largely due to the limitations of conventional experimental pipelines and the growing biological complexity of the pathogen. In recent years, computational drug discovery approaches-including virtual screening, artificial intelligence (AI)-driven modeling, and hybrid computational frameworks-have substantially expanded the chemical space accessible for early-stage anti-TB research. However, their translational success remains limited. This discrepancy reflects a fundamental mismatch between target-centric computational paradigms and the multi-scale biological constraints of Mtb, including permeability barriers, efflux mechanisms, metabolic state heterogeneity, lesion-level pharmacokinetics, and regimen-dependent therapeutic effects. This review critically evaluates current computational strategies for anti-TB drug screening, with particular emphasis on their performance under TB-specific biological and resistance constraints. We further explore computational approaches designed to address drug-resistant Mtb, including resistance-aware compound design, host-directed therapy, and combination regimen modeling. Finally, we explore key limitations in current computational pipelines, including challenges in data quality, biological integration, and regimen-level modeling, and propose a shift toward biologically grounded, regimen-aware, and systems-level frameworks. Bridging the gap between in silico prediction and clinical efficacy will require integrating multi-scale biological realism into computational pipelines, enabling more reliable translation of computational advances into effective anti-TB therapeutics.

articles.title: Context-dependent mTOR pharmacology in atherosclerotic plaque stability and exposure-guided modulation.
articles.abstract: Despite advances in lipid lowering, anti-inflammatory therapy and revascularization, residual cardiovascular risk may partly reflect persistent lesion-level inflammation and defective plaque repair that are not fully corrected by systemic risk-factor control. The mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) integrates inflammatory, metabolic and reparative programmes, but its effects vary with cell state, plaque niche, complex identity, and signalling amplitude and duration. Evidence is strongest for context-dependent macrophage mTOR signalling, yet macrophage/myeloid mTORC2 disruption has produced opposing lesion phenotypes across genetic models; endothelial and smooth-muscle evidence remains less direct. Pharmacological, genetic and lesion-directed delivery studies demonstrate that mTOR perturbation can modify experimental atherosclerosis. However, genetic perturbation cannot be equated with rapalog pharmacology, and existing studies do not yet define cell-resolved exposure-engagement-response relationships and relate them to plaque composition. This evidential asymmetry limits interpretation of whether broad or prolonged mTOR inhibition can selectively suppress disease-amplifying outputs while preserving homeostatic programmes. In this Review, focused primarily on lipid-rich, rupture-prone plaques and using rapalogs as the principal pharmacological model, we apply an exposure-guided pharmacological framework to distinguish administered dose from lesion exposure, cellular availability, target engagement and pharmacodynamic recovery. Compartment-resolved PK-PD studies, cell-specific pathway interrogation and large-animal validation will be needed to quantify these relationships and determine whether maladaptive mTOR outputs can be suppressed without compromising vascular repair.

articles.title: Lactate-associated fibroblast-macrophage signaling in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis: evidence boundaries and immunopharmacological opportunities.
articles.abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is characterized by recurrent alveolar epithelial injury, maladaptive repair, fibroblast activation, and extracellular-matrix accumulation. Lactate metabolism is increasingly implicated in communication between stromal and immune cells in fibrotic lung niches through monocarboxylate transporter (MCT)-mediated transport, hydroxycarboxylic acid receptor 1 (HCAR1/GPR81) sensing, extracellular acidification, and lysine lactylation. This narrative review evaluates the evidence for directional lactate-associated fibroblast-macrophage signaling, the limits of proposed reciprocal interactions, and their therapeutic implications. Human IPF observations, experimental pulmonary-fibrosis studies, and indirect evidence from other disease contexts are separated according to disease relevance and causal resolution. The strongest direct mechanistic evidence supports lactate released by activated myofibroblasts as a stimulus for macrophage histone lactylation and profibrotic transcription, whereas reciprocal macrophage-to-fibroblast lactate feedback remains unproven. Among the lactate-associated targets reviewed, fibroblast-associated MCT4 currently has the most developed preclinical evidence package, supported by disease-relevant observations, target perturbation, and antifibrotic activity in experimental models. However, no lactate-directed therapeutic strategy has yet demonstrated clinical efficacy in IPF. HCAR1/GPR81, lactate-production pathways, and lactylation-associated machinery remain mechanistically compelling but are at earlier stages of pharmacological validation. Overall, available evidence is more consistent with lactate functioning as a context-dependent amplifier or maintenance signal than with a demonstrated uniform initiating role in IPF. Lactate-directed interventions may therefore be considered adjunctive strategies alongside established antifibrotic therapy. Further translation will require cell- and disease-stage-specific causal validation, lesion-resolved target engagement, efficacy in established fibrosis, and a therapeutic window that preserves physiological lactate metabolism.

articles.title: Engineering aptamer-based therapeutics for precision cancer immunotherapy: from molecular targeting to clinical applications.
articles.abstract: Although cancer immunotherapy has revolutionized cancer therapy, the clinical efficacy of this approach is restricted due to tumor heterogeneity, immune escape, therapeutic resistance, poor tumor penetration, and toxic side effects. Short single-stranded DNA or RNA oligonucleotides, termed aptamers, have high affinity for a given target, low immunogenicity, and high chemical programmability and are emerging as promising agents for precision cancer therapies and immuno-oncology. This review aims to provide a comprehensive, integrated overview of the development of aptamer-based cancer therapeutics, from molecular engineering and pharmacology to clinical applications and translational potential. The discovery and optimization of tumor and immune-specific aptamers have been enhanced by the development of conventional SELEX, Cell-SELEX, in vivo SELEX, high-throughput sequencing, microfluidic selection, and AI-assisted selection. To enhance nuclease resistance, circulation time, biodistribution, and tumor accumulation, chemical modifications such as PEGylation, 2'-fluoro, 2'-O-methyl, LNAs, phosphorothioate linkages, circularization, and lipid/albumin binding have been developed. Aptamers can directly regulate oncogenic and immune signaling pathways or be used as targeted delivery vehicles for chemotherapeutic drugs, siRNAs, miRNAs, proteins, peptides, and CRISPR-based systems. Moreover, aptamers targeting tumor-associated biomarkers, cancer stem cells, the tumor vasculature, stromal components, and immune regulatory pathways have the potential to selectively remodel the tumor microenvironment. In addition, they are well-suited to other immunotherapy strategies, including immune checkpoint inhibitors, chemotherapy, radiotherapy, photodynamic or photothermal therapy, oncolytic viruses, and cancer vaccines, thereby further supporting a multifunctional, personalized treatment approach. Although there has been significant progress in pre-clinical research, several issues remain regarding pharmacokinetics, tumor penetration, off-target effects, manufacturing, long-term safety, regulatory approval, and clinical validation. Additional advancements in aptamer engineering, nanotechnology, computational design, and biomarker-directed therapy could potentially enable the development of these platforms into successful next-generation precision cancer immunotherapies.

articles.title: Translational lipidomics in glaucoma: mechanisms, biomarkers, and therapeutic horizons.
articles.abstract: Glaucoma is a multifactorial optic neuropathy. Intraocular pressure (IOP), aging, vascular dysregulation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial failure, and chronic neuroinflammation converge on retinal ganglion cell (RGC) degeneration and optic nerve damage. Lipid mediators are central to this biology, linking membrane remodeling to aqueous humor (AH) dynamics, glial activation, vascular tone, extracellular matrix turnover, and neuronal survival. Lipidomics has widened the field beyond prostaglandin pharmacology to include oxylipins, lysophospholipids, sphingolipids, endocannabinoids, and specialized pro-resolving mediators (SPMs). Human studies in AH, tears, and plasma report reproducible perturbations in arachidonic acid (AA) metabolism, oxidized linoleate products, phosphatidylcholines, lysophosphatidylcholines, sphingomyelins, and ceramides; experimental models further implicate ceramide accumulation, phospholipase A2 activation, cyclooxygenase signaling, endocannabinoid tone, and failed inflammation resolution in retinal injury. Recent work also shows that latanoprost itself induces an aqueous-humor AA/LXA4 circuit in glaucoma patients, indicating that established prostaglandin therapy may engage endogenous resolution pathways and complicate the interpretation of treated-cohort lipidomic studies. This review covers the mechanistic roles of lipid mediators in IOP regulation, TM dysfunction, neuroinflammation, and neurodegeneration; the emerging biomarker literature in AH, tears, and plasma; and potential therapeutic directions, including soluble epoxide hydrolase (sEH) inhibition, sphingolipid modulation, endocannabinoid augmentation, and SPM-based neuroprotection. We conclude with the main barriers to translation: small ocular sample volumes, treatment confounding, limited longitudinal data, and the need for disease-subtype stratification.

articles.title: Cross-organ translation of antifibrotic strategies from skin and lung fibrosis to glaucoma filtration surgery.
articles.abstract: Filtering bleb scarring after glaucoma filtration surgery (GFS) remains the leading cause of surgical failure, and current antimetabolites are limited by non-selective cytotoxicity that restricts their long-term use. Research on skin and lung fibrosis has accumulated extensive experience in antifibrotic mechanisms and therapeutic approaches. These tissues share a common transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β)-driven program of fibroblast activation and extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling with Tenon capsule fibroblasts, providing a theoretical basis for translating antifibrotic strategies across organs. From a cross-organ translational medicine perspective, this review systematically summarizes progress in translating antifibrotic research from skin and lung fibrosis to antiscarring therapy for GFS, focusing on four aspects: shared fibrotic mechanisms; repurposed approved drugs and emerging molecular targets; local drug delivery systems (DDS); and ophthalmology-specific translational challenges. It also highlights mechanotransduction via Yes-associated protein (YAP)/transcriptional co-activator with PDZ-binding motif (TAZ), lysyl oxidase (LOX)-mediated ECM crosslinking, and the translational potential of local sustained-release delivery in filtering blebs. Building on this foundation, we propose that multi-target combination therapy, precision local delivery, and individualized antiscarring strategies based on biomarkers such as aqueous humor TGF-β2 may represent important future directions for improving the long-term success rate of GFS.

articles.title: Adipose-derived stem cell extracellular vesicles in diabetic microangiopathy: from pathological networks to clinical translation.
articles.abstract: Diabetic microangiopathy (DMA) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in diabetes. Its pathogenesis involves interconnected processes, including metabolic disturbance, oxidative stress, inflammation, immune dysregulation, endothelial dysfunction, mitochondrial abnormalities, and impaired tissue repair. This complexity suggests that therapeutic strategies targeting individual pathways may be insufficient to address the multidimensional pathological processes underlying DMA. Adipose-derived stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles (ADSC-EVs) have emerged as potential cell-free therapeutic candidates whose multimolecular cargo may modulate multiple disease-relevant processes. Preclinical evidence suggests that ADSC-EVs can influence oxidative stress, inflammation, angiogenesis, immune responses, and tissue repair, providing a potential basis for multitarget modulation of pathological microenvironments. This review critically evaluates organ-specific evidence for ADSC-EVs in diabetic retinopathy, diabetic kidney disease, diabetic peripheral neuropathy, and diabetic chronic wounds, with particular attention to evidence specificity, therapeutic mechanisms, delivery barriers, and translational limitations. We further summarize advances in EV engineering, including parent-cell and cargo engineering, surface modification, biomaterial integration, and stimuli-responsive delivery, while distinguishing ADSC-EV-specific findings from evidence extrapolated from the broader EV field. Finally, we discuss major barriers to clinical translation, including manufacturing standardization, potency assessment, biodistribution, organ-specific delivery, long-term safety, and regulatory evaluation. Future studies integrating disease stratification, multi-omics, rational engineering, and standardized manufacturing may help determine whether the multitarget effects of ADSC-EVs can be translated into reproducible and clinically meaningful therapies for DMA.

articles.title: The role of the JAK/STAT pathway in the pathogenesis and treatment of post-COVID autoimmune syndromes.
articles.abstract: The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic has not only resulted in acute respiratory illness but has also led to a growing population of individuals affected by persistent, debilitating symptoms, collectively known as post-COVID syndrome or "Long COVID". This condition presents with a variety of manifestations, including fatigue, joint pain, cognitive disturbances, and dysautonomia, often mimicking autoimmune and neuroinflammatory disorders. Recent research highlights the Janus kinase/signal transducer and activator of transcription (JAK/STAT) signalling pathway as a central mediator in the inflammatory cascade triggered by SARS-CoV-2 infection. This review explores the dual role of the JAK/STAT pathway in both the acute phase of COVID-19 and its potential contribution to post-infectious autoimmune phenomena. We summarize the current understanding of JAK inhibitors (JAKi) as therapeutic agents for mitigating hyperinflammation during active infection and examine their emerging role in the management of post-COVID syndromes, particularly in cases with pulmonary involvement and features overlapping with fibromyalgia and chronic fatigue syndrome. Moreover, we discuss the safety profile of JAKi, their impact on vaccine immunogenicity, and the implications of autoantibody formation targeting the autonomic nervous system. Understanding the immunopathological mechanisms underpinning post-COVID may not only inform therapeutic strategies but also illuminate broader pathways involved in chronic autoimmune conditions.

articles.title: Ranking rather than predicting: what optimised T-cell assays can tell us about the immunogenicity of biologics.
Cyclodextrin-formulated ferrocifen penetrates the brain and significantly improves survival in an orthotopic mouse model of glioblastoma.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Despite intensive chemotherapeutic and radiotherapeutic approaches for its treatment, glioblastoma (GBM) remains incurable, in part due to the difficulty of active molecules in crossing the blood-brain-barrier (BBB). Developing a suitable formulation for molecules with promising in vitro anticancer activity thus represents an essential step toward their in vivo translation. METHODS: We report here the formulation of the lipophilic compound P15, a ferrocenyl analog of hydroxytamoxifen with broad antiproliferative activity, in randomly methylated β-cyclodextrin (RAMEB), together with the extensive characterization of the inclusion complex, pharmacokinetic (PK) studies, and an in vivo efficacy study in an orthotopic model of human glioblastoma in mice. RESULTS: Inclusion of P15 as its citrate salt is significantly more efficient, with a 5 mM solution of RAMEB being able to solubilize 12 times more P15-cit than P15. The inclusion complex P15-cit@RAMEB exhibits a favorable stability constant on the order of 104 M-1, as determined from the phase solubility diagram. The inclusion complex is characterized by a 2:1 host:guest ratio, with that the ferrocenyl moiety inserted into one of the cyclodextrins while the other incorporates an aromatic ring. PK analyses suggest a marked biodistribution of P15 in the mouse brain following IV administration of P15-cit@RAMEB at 20 mg/kg. Crucially, the survival of orthotopic GBM-bearing mice is significantly improved, resulting in 17-33% long-term survivors. RNA sequencing analysis of treated mouse brains compared with controls reveals that the treatment is associated with the inhibition of pathways related to angiogenesis, metal ion homeostasis and calcium signaling. CONCLUSIONS: Formulation of the citrate form of P15 in RAMEB represents a promising strategy for developing a more effective therapy for GBM patients.

articles.title: Brexpiprazole, a third-generation atypical antipsychotic inhibits voltage-gated K+ channels in rabbit coronary artery smooth muscle cells.
articles.abstract: Voltage-gated K+ (Kv) channels are crucial for regulating membrane potential and contractility in vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs). In this study, we investigated the effects of the third-generation antipsychotic brexpiprazole on Kv channels in native VSMCs isolated from rabbit coronary arteries. Brexpiprazole inhibited Kv currents in a concentration-dependent manner, with an IC50 of 8.35 ± 2.61 μM and a Hill coefficient of 0.81 ± 0.07. This inhibition was accompanied by an accelerated inactivation rate and a leftward shift of the steady-state inactivation curve. Repetitive stimulation at 1 and 2 Hz enhanced the inhibitory effect, and recovery from inactivation was significantly prolonged, indicating use-dependent blockade. Pharmacological analysis further implied subtype specificity, as inhibition was attenuated by pretreatment with diphenyl phosphine oxide-1 (a Kv1.5-selective blocker) but not by stromatoxin-1 (Kv2.1) or linopirdine (Kv7). Taken together, these findings indicate that Kv1.5 contributes to the brexpiprazole-sensitive Kv current and that brexpiprazole suppresses Kv currents through both concentration- and state-dependent mechanisms, at least in part by altering channel inactivation properties.

articles.title: CYP26A1 is involved in neuropathic pain through RXRβ-mediated neuronal excitability and neuroinflammation in the DRG.
articles.abstract: Neuropathic pain remains a challenging clinical problem with limited therapeutic options. As the key enzyme responsible for catabolizing all-trans-retinoic acid (RA), CYP26A1 is crucial for maintaining RA homeostasis, yet its role in neuropathic pain remains unclear. In this study, we report that spinal nerve ligation (SNL) increased CYP26A1 expression in dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons. Both local DRG injection of CYP26A1-targeting siRNA and talarozole, a specific CYP26A1 inhibitor, significantly attenuated SNL-induced mechanical allodynia and thermal hyperalgesia. At the molecular level, CYP26A1 inhibition shifted the local cytokine balance, suppressing the pro-inflammatory cytokines TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 while upregulating the anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10 within the DRG. Electrophysiological recordings further revealed that talarozole treatment reduced the hyperexcitability of DRG neurons in SNL mice. Moreover, SNL induced dysregulation of RA receptor expression in DRG neurons, characterized by increased RA receptor alpha (RARα) and decreased retinoid X receptor beta (RXRβ). In addition, DRG-specific overexpression of RXRβ not only alleviated mechanical allodynia and thermal hyperalgesia but also inhibited pro-inflammatory cytokine expression and reduced neuronal hyperexcitability in SNL mice. Collectively, our findings reveal that inhibiting CYP26A1 or restoring RXRβ expression in the DRG can alleviate neuropathic pain by reducing the neuroinflammatory response and suppressing neuronal hyperexcitability. Thus, targeting the CYP26A1/RXRβ signaling may represent a novel therapeutic strategy for neuropathic pain.

articles.title: Tabersonine-mediated inhibition of the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway modulates macrophage reprogramming and alleviates osteoarthritis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a common degenerative joint disease primarily marked by cartilage breakdown, with synovitis driving disease progression. During disease exacerbation, macrophages in synovial tissue predominantly polarize to the M1 phenotype. Tabersonine (TAB), derived from Catharanthus roseus, exhibits anti-inflammatory properties, yet its exact mechanism in osteoarthritis remains elusive. PURPOSE: In vitro and in vivo experiments were performed to evaluate the effects of TAB on macrophage inflammatory responses and OA-related cartilage changes. METHODS: The experimental design included LPS stimulation of RAW264.7 cells for quantitative analysis of inflammatory mediator production. TAB's effect on macrophage polarization was assessed by immunofluorescence, Western blot, and flow cytometry. Treated cells were cultured together with ATDC5 chondrocytes to assess extracellular matrix synthesis and degradation-related molecule expression. In vivo, osteoarthritis was induced in rat knees via anterior cruciate ligament transection (ACLT) to assess TAB's role in joint degeneration. RESULTS: In vitro experiments showed that TAB effectively inhibited LPS-induced macrophage inflammation and promoted macrophage reprogramming toward an M2-like phenotype. Transcriptome analysis demonstrated that TAB inhibited the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway in macrophages stimulated by LPS. Cell studies demonstrated that TAB regulated M1/M2 polarization via PI3K/AKT inhibition and enhanced the production of cartilage regeneration-related molecules. In vivo, TAB attenuated cartilage degeneration in ACLT rats. CONCLUSIONS: TAB protects cartilage by modulating macrophage reprogramming and inhibiting chondrocyte extracellular matrix degradation through the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway.

articles.title: Chronic Topical Water-Soluble Cannabidiol Formulation Reduces Intraocular Pressure and Corneal Mechanical Sensitivity in DBA/2J Mice.
articles.abstract: Glaucoma is a multifactorial neurodegenerative disease and a leading cause of irreversible blindness worldwide. Although elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) is the main modifiable risk factor, current therapies often fail to fully prevent disease progression and may cause ocular discomfort. Cannabidiol (CBD) has attracted increasing interest due to its anti-inflammatory, analgesic and vasoregulatory properties, yet its ocular effects remain controversial, partly due to formulation-dependent limitations and short-term administration paradigms. We evaluated a novel water-soluble topical CBD formulation in a spontaneous murine model of glaucoma (DBA/2J mice), using CD-1 mice as a non-glaucomatous comparator strain. IOP, tear production, corneal mechanical sensitivity and body weight were assessed longitudinally in conscious animals following acute and chronic CBD administration (once or twice daily). Contralateral untreated eyes were analyzed to investigate potential systemic or bilateral effects. Following an initial transient IOP increase, topical CBD progressively induced a significant and sustained reduction of IOP in the treated eyes of DBA/2J mice, particularly during chronic twice-daily administration. IOP changes in contralateral eyes were smaller and inconsistent, supporting a predominantly local ocular effect. CBD also increased corneal touch threshold in DBA/2J mice, indicating reduced corneal mechanical sensitivity, with effects persisting after treatment withdrawal. Tear production and body weight were not significantly affected in either strain, suggesting good ocular and systemic tolerability. Overall, chronic topical administration of a water-soluble CBD formulation lowered IOP and modulated corneal sensitivity in a strain-dependent manner. These findings support CBD as a potential adjunctive therapeutic strategy targeting both ocular hypertension and sensory dysfunction.

articles.title: β-Amyrin,an active compound of Bryophyllum pinnatum,alleviates alcoholic liver disease by regulating AKT1 expression and enhancing antioxidant defense.
articles.abstract: Bryophyllum pinnatum (L. f.) Oken (BP), a traditional hepatoprotective herb, has demonstrated therapeutic potential in managing liver disorders. However, the specific bioactive compounds of BP and its mechanisms against alcoholic liver disease (ALD) remain unclear. In this study, the bioactive compounds of BP were screened by database mining and their targets were predicted. A compound-target-disease network was constructed to identify core targets, followed by molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulation to validate the binding of β-Amyrin with AKT1. The hepatoprotective efficacy and mechanism were finally verified in ethanol-exposed HepG2 cells. A database screening process has identified four bioactive compounds (β-Amyrin, Astragalin, α-Amyrin and Bryophyllin A). Network pharmacology analyses revealed 138 common targets, primarily associated with lipid metabolism, hepatitis B and C, and the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway, and core targets included AKT1, CCND1, EGFR, HIF1A and SRC. Notably, in vitro experiments using ethanol-exposed HepG2 cells demonstrated that β-Amyrin significantly reduced transaminase (ALT, AST), total cholesterol (TC) and triglyceride (TG). Additionally, β-Amyrin enhanced antioxidant defense (SOD, CAT, GSH) and suppressed malondialdehyde (MDA) accumulation. Furthermore, β-Amyrin alleviated intracellular lipid accumulation as evidenced by Oil Red O staining. Mechanistically, β-Amyrin restored the expression of total AKT1 and its phosphorylation level (p-AKT1), which could be abolished by AKT1-specific inhibitor MK2206. This is the first study to identify β-Amyrin as the key bioactive compound of BP against ALD, and these findings provide compelling evidence for BP's potential as a therapeutic strategy for ALD.

articles.title: HSPB1 in Dorsal Hippocampal Astrocytes Contributes to Stress-Induced Reinstatement of Methamphetamine Conditioned Place Preference.
articles.abstract: Methamphetamine (MA) addiction is a chronic neuropsychiatric disorder characterized by compulsive drug-seeking behavior and a high relapse risk driven by the persistent retrieval of reward-associated memories. Although astrocytes are increasingly recognized as important modulators of drug-associated behaviors and reward memories, their contributions to MA-associated contextual memory remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigated the role of dorsal hippocampal CA1 (dCA1) astrocytes in a stress-induced reinstatement model of MA conditioned place preference (CPP) in female mice. Reinstatement of MA CPP elevated expression of astrocytic markers GFAP and S100β and enhanced Ca2+ signals in dCA1 astrocytes. Chemogenetic inhibition of dCA1 astrocytes significantly attenuated CPP reinstatement. Proteomic profiling of hippocampal tissue revealed heat shock protein beta-1 (HSPB1) as a differentially expressed protein during reinstatement. Subsequent immunohistochemical and immunofluorescence analyses revealed increased HSPB1 immunoreactivity in the dCA1 and its predominant colocalization with GFAP-positive astrocytes. Notably, pharmacological inhibition of HSPB1 using the J2 inhibitor, or GFAP-promoter-driven HSPB1 knockdown robustly suppressed stress-induced reinstatement of MA CPP. These findings reveal that HSPB1 in dCA1 astrocytes contributes to stress-induced reinstatement of MA-associated contextual preference.

articles.title: Neuroprotective Effects of Remdesivir in ICV-STZ Induced Alzheimer-Like Pathology: Potential Involvement of ACE2-Associated Signaling.
articles.abstract: Alzheimer's disease involves interacting metabolic, oxidative, and inflammatory disturbances, with accumulating evidence implicating dysregulation of the brain renin-angiotensin system in disease-related pathology. This study investigated the neuroprotective effects of remdesivir against intracerebroventricular streptozotocin (ICV-STZ)-induced Alzheimer-like pathology and examined the potential involvement of ACE1/ACE2-associated signaling. Following ICV-STZ administration on Days 1 and 3, remdesivir treatment was initiated on Day 4 and continued once daily through Day 31. Remdesivir was evaluated using molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, behavioral testing, cholinesterase inhibition assays, biochemical analyses, ELISA, immunohistochemistry, qRT-PCR, Western blotting, and histopathology. ICV-STZ induced memory-related and affective-like behavioral impairments, altered exploratory activity, reduced ACE2 expression, increased ACE1 expression, oxidative stress, NLRP3/NF-κB-associated neuroinflammation, amyloid/tau-related alterations, and neuronal degeneration. Remdesivir dose-dependently improved behavioral and biochemical outcomes, increased ACE2 expression, reduced ACE1 expression, and attenuated neuroinflammation, oxidative injury, and neurodegeneration, with the most pronounced effects observed at 30 mg/kg. Pharmacological modulation with DX600 and diminazene aceturate altered the protective effects of remdesivir, providing supportive but not definitive evidence for the involvement of ACE2-associated signaling. However, ACE2 enzymatic activity and downstream Ang-(1-7)/Mas receptor signaling were not directly assessed. Remdesivir also inhibited AChE and BChE, with IC50 values of 237.4 μM and 535.7 μM, respectively. These findings demonstrate that early remdesivir intervention attenuates the development of ICV-STZ-induced Alzheimer-like pathology and suggest that modulation of the ACE1/ACE2 expression balance may be associated with its antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and neuroprotective effects.

articles.title: Dissolution coning in USP apparatus II - Part I: quantifying formulation-dependent coning severity with the drug entrapment fraction (DEF).
articles.abstract: Dissolution coning is the accumulation of disintegrated particles beneath the paddle in USP Apparatus II that can confound dissolution interpretation due to drug retention within the deposit. Visual qualitative observations or hydrodynamic suspension criteria, such as no-coning rpm (NCrpm), do not measure the impact of coning on drug release. Hence, coning behavior across different tablet formulations is examined in Part I with an intent to propose a quantitative metric to classify its severity. Immediate-release ibuprofen (BCS Class II) tablets formulated with microcrystalline cellulose (MCC; Avicel pH 102) or three grades of dibasic calcium phosphate anhydrous (Fujicalin, A-Tab, Calipharm A) at drug loadings (DL) of 20, 50, and 70% w/w were considered. Distinct dissolution responses were observed, ranging from complete release despite cones for MCC to substantial drug entrapment (Fujicalin < A-Tab < Calipharm A), even with comparable or lower NCrpm. Coning severity could not be explained by particle size or terminal settling velocity. Consequently, the extent of incomplete dissolution characterized as drug entrapment fraction (DEF) was used for the first time as a quantitative metric to quantify coning severity. DEF enabled linking cone formation with dissolution performance, providing a formulation-relevant measure of coning severity. It exhibited distinct trends among the excipient systems and increased as the drug: filler ratio decreased. This trend was qualitatively consistent with visible cone and surrounding zone structure where higher-DEF formulations exhibited more compact clearly defined cones. Overall, DEF is demonstrated as a quantitative metric to distinguish formulation dependent coning behavior and severity.

articles.title: Formulation of orodispersible live biotherapeutic products using spray-freeze-drying as bulk formulation production process.
articles.abstract: Spray freeze drying (SFD) was evaluated as bulk production process in the development of orodispersible probiotic tablets. The technology encompasses spray freezing into cold vapour followed by rotational bulk freeze drying. Three nozzle diameters, i.e. 220 µm, 300 µm and 400 µm, were used to produce fresh probiotic bulk powder, yielding microspherical particles with respective diameters of 385 µm, 556 µm and 654 µm. The SFD formulation consisted out of trehalose, PBS and probiotic cells. Subsequently, these powders were used in a compaction simulator to investigate their compressability and tabletting behaviour. Round flat-faced tablets were manufactured using a die with a diameter of 10 mm, and the fill volume was set to obtain a tablet mass of about 275 mg. The uniaxial compaction force was varied from 1.0 kN up to 10.0 kN in incremental steps of 1.0 kN, corresponding to compaction pressures ranging from 12.7 to 127.3 MPa. Heckel analysis revealed a yield pressure of 102 MPa when compacting the SFD powders.
