Moreover, low compaction force of only 28.2 MPa should be applied to obtain tablets of acceptable tablet tensile strength of 1.7 MPa, suited for further processing according to industrial standards. The low compaction pressure contributed to the stability of the bacterial cells during storage, with a final bacterial concentration in the tablets of 7.7 log CFU/g after 6 months of storage at 4 °C. A slight compaction force appeared to benefit the stability compared to the loose powder state. Furthermore, the compacts' disintegration time at the recommended TTS of 1.7 MPa appeared to be below 60 s. In conclusion, these findings validate the novel application of SFD bulk powders in tableting processes, proving SFD to be a viable and robust formulation strategy for probiotic tablets.

articles.title: A tumor-responsive p53-loaded nanovesicle system for senescence induction and immune microenvironment reprogramming.
articles.abstract: The tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) critically regulates the balance between antitumor immunity and immune evasion. Although cellular senescence can promote immune-mediated tumor clearance through the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), this mechanism is frequently compromised by loss of p53 function, particularly in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). Consequently, strategies capable of restoring p53 activity while harnessing intact immune-responsive pathways are urgently needed. Integrated transcriptomic analyses provided a computational basis for this therapeutic strategy. Bulk RNA-seq demonstrated that, in TNBC, the downstream SASP-immune activation axis remains largely preserved, whereas the upstream p53-SASP coupling is disrupted, supporting the concept that exogenous p53 restoration may effectively re-engage immune programs. Single-cell RNA-seq further revealed that p53-functional malignant cells exhibit enhanced tumor-immune communication and immune-recognition signals, reinforcing the feasibility of p53 reactivation to remodel the TIME. Guided by these insights, we engineered a dual-functional, tumor-responsive nanovesicle system for p53 delivery. Escherichia coli was genetically modified to express p53, and p53-loaded outer membrane vesicles (OMV@p53) were coated with a biomimetic calcium phosphate shell via bionanomorphic mineralization, yielding acid-responsive nanovesicles (Ca@OMV@p53; 200-300 nm). This coating enhanced biocompatibility and enabled pH-triggered release within the mildly acidic tumor microenvironment. In vitro, Ca@OMV@p53 efficiently induced tumor cell senescence and promoted M1 macrophage polarization. In vivo, treatment markedly increased intratumoral infiltration of M1 macrophages and cytotoxic T lymphocytes, accompanied by elevated pro-inflammatory cytokines and sustained immune activation. Together, this study demonstrates that p53-restoration via a tumor-responsive nanodelivery system can synergistically induce senescence and immune-mediated tumor clearance. By integrating systems-level bioinformatics with experimental nanomedicine, our work establishes a rational framework for senescence-based immunomodulatory cancer therapy.

articles.title: Antibacterial, antibiofilm, mucus penetration properties and pulmonary biocompatibility of inhalable spray-dried levofloxacin-ambroxol composite microparticles.
articles.abstract: This study evaluated the antibacterial and biofilm-disruption activities of spray-dried levofloxacin (LVX) and ambroxol (AMB) composite dry powder inhaler (DPI) formulations against laboratory and clinical strains of P. aeruginosa and a clinical S. aureus strain. Cytotoxicity and pro-inflammatory activity of the formulations were investigated in THP-1 derived macrophages, healthy and COPD bronchial epithelial cells (HBE), and mucus penetration using an artificial mucus model. Spray dried LVX retained antibacterial activity against PA14 (MIC50 0.075-0.099 µg/mL versus 0.076 µg/mL for free LVX), whereas free AMB showed no antibacterial activity. Formulations containing higher AMB proportions, exhibited greater antibacterial activity than free LVX against AUST-02 and 2.1. The developed formulations also enhanced biofilm disruption against PA14 and AUST-02. AMB improved penetration of spray-dried LVX, particularly with F4 (LVX:AMB 1:1 with 5 % leucine) showing statistically significant (p < 0.05) penetration enhancement compared to free LVX (60.8 % and 82.8 % in 2 h) at 16 µg/mL. All formulations maintained high cell viability (>83 %) in THP-1 macrophages, while no significant cytotoxicity or increase in IL-8 production was observed. Overall, the prepared composite antibiotic microparticles demonstrated superior antibacterial activity against the tested clinical strains, enhanced biofilm disruption and LVX mucus penetration, while preserving pulmonary biocompatibility in the tested cell models.

articles.title: RSP1141, a reversible non-covalent BTK inhibitor, suppresses GPVI-mediated platelet activation.
articles.abstract: AIMS: The glycoprotein VI (GPVI)-Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK) axis drives collagen-induced platelet activation and arterial thrombosis. Approved BTK inhibitors act irreversibly on Cys481, raising concerns over off-target kinase inhibition, C481S resistance, and bleeding. We aimed to identify a non-covalent, reversible BTK inhibitor with antiplatelet activity and to define quantitatively its selectivity within the platelet GPVI cascade. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Fifty-five imidazo[4,5-b]pyridine derivatives were screened using a BTK enzymatic assay and CRP-XL-induced aggregation of washed human platelets. The lead compound, RSP1141, was characterized by concentration-response immunoblotting of GPVI signaling nodes, Ca2+ mobilization, functional assays, drug washout, 370-kinase profiling, C481S enzymatic assay, molecular docking, and a murine FeCl₃-induced arterial thrombosis and tail-bleeding model. KEY FINDINGS: RSP1141 inhibited BTK (IC₅₀ 27.9 nM) and CRP-XL-induced aggregation (IC₅₀ 173.6 nM). In intact platelets, RSP1141 inhibited BTK-pY223 (IC₅₀ 0.316 μM) and PLCγ2-pY753 (0.325 μM) at essentially identical concentrations, whereas SYK-pY525/526 (2.88 μM) and Src-family kinase-pY416 (3.96 μM) required 9.1- and 12.5-fold higher concentrations. Downstream PKC, Ca2+, granule secretion, integrin, and spreading responses were suppressed. RSP1141 retained activity against C481S BTK (IC₅₀ 141 nM), docking predicted no covalent Cys481 engagement, and platelet aggregation and BTK-PLCγ2 signaling recovered after washout. In mice, oral RSP1141 delayed FeCl₃-induced carotid occlusion at 10 mg/kg, whereas tail bleeding time was not detectably prolonged. SIGNIFICANCE: RSP1141 engages the BTK-PLCγ2 node with approximately 10-fold cellular selectivity over proximal GPVI kinases, inhibits reversibly, and is antithrombotic in vivo without detectable bleeding prolongation, providing a mechanistically differentiated antiplatelet lead.

articles.title: Curdione restores brain-spleen axis-mediated Th1/Th2 immune homeostasis via modulation of LCN2 to alleviate CUMS-induced depressive-like behaviors in mice.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Curcuma wenyujin Y.H.Chen & C.Ling supplies both Curcumae Rhizoma (the rhizome) and Curcumae Radix (the root tuber). Curcumae Radix is documented in the Chinese Pharmacopoeia (2020) for moving qi, relieving depression and clearing the heart, and is used in classic formulas such as Baijin Wan to treat depression-like syndromes. Curdione is a major sesquiterpenoid constituent of this species. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to investigate the mechanism underlying curdione-mediated amelioration of depressive-like behaviors in CUMS-exposed mice, and to elucidate the core role of LCN2 and the brain-spleen axis in this process. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A CUMS-induced mouse depression model was established, with interventions including splenic sympathetic denervation (SDN) and administration of the LCN2 inhibitor ZINC00640089. Assessments were conducted via behavioral tests (OFT; EPMT; TST; MWM), histopathology, ELISA, flow cytometry, qRT-PCR, Western blot and transcriptomics. RESULTS: CUMS exposure significantly induced depressive-like behaviors, hippocampal neuronal injury, splenic atrophy and Th1/Th2 immune deviation (elevated IFN-γ, decreased IL-4 and IL-5) in mice, which were effectively reversed by SDN. Curdione ameliorated depressive-like behaviors, and restored Th1/Th2 balance. Transcriptomic screening and experimental validation identified LCN2 as a candidate key mediator; curdione significantly downregulated its aberrant overexpression in both the hippocampus and spleen. Pharmacological inhibition of LCN2 mimicked the antidepressant and immunomodulatory effects of curdione. CONCLUSION: Curdione exerts antidepressant effects by indirectly modulating LCN2 to restore brain-spleen axis-mediated Th1/Th2 immune homeostasis. These findings not only support the involvement of LCN2 in the pathogenesis of depression, but also validate the therapeutic potential of modulating neuro-immune crosstalk mediators, supporting the development of curdione as a promising natural antidepressant agent. Our findings further provide modern pharmacological evidence supporting the traditional antidepressant use of Curcuma wenyujin.

articles.title: Mechanism of Sini Decoction and its self-assembled component in improving Doxorubicin-induced cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract: ETHOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Sini decoction (SND) is a typical Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) prescription composed of Aconitum carmichaelii Debx, Zingiberis Rhizoma, and Glycyrrhizae Radix et Rhizoma Praeparate cum Melle, used to treat cardiomyopathy in TCM clinical trials. Recent studies have shown that the active ingredients of SND can form self-assembled complexes during decoction, whose bioactivity differs from that of the monomeric compound. However, current research on the active ingredients of SND has not yet included these self-assembled components, and the mechanism by which SND exerts its effects on doxorubicin (Dox)-induced cardiomyopathy remains unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to investigate the underlying mechanisms by which SND and its self-assembled component (SAC) improve Dox-induced cardiomyopathy in mice. The complete isolation of the self-assembled complex component from SND was achieved for the first time, and its activity and mechanism were explored, providing a new perspective for revealing the substance basis of TCM prescriptions. MATERIALS AND METHODS: SAC and the unassembled component (SMC) were separated from SND by ultrafiltration, and UHPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS was used to qualitatively analyze their chemical components. Based on the main components of SAC, Benzoylmesaconine-glycyrrhizic acid complex (GBMA) was prepared under simulated decoction conditions of SND. A mouse model of cardiomyopathy was established by intraperitoneal injection of Dox, followed by oral administration of SND, SAC, SMC, and GBMA, to evaluate improvements in cardiac systolic function across treatment groups. The effects of SND and its components on cardiac systolic function were evaluated to reveal the differences in their medicinal effects. The mechanisms by which SND and SAC improve cardiomyopathy were systematically investigated using Seahorse energy metabolism analysis, autophagic flux analysis, and Western blotting, with a focus on the interconnected organelles, mitochondria, and autophagosomes. RESULTS: A total of 173 compounds were identified in SAC. Among them, molecules with lower hydrophilicity tend to self-assemble in the decoction, while molecules with a molecular weight less than 300 Da participate less in self-assembly. SND, SAC, and GBMA significantly improved abnormal cardiac systolic function in Dox-induced cardiomyopathy mice, while SMC had no such effects. SAC and GBMA inhibited Dox-induced excessive mitophagy by downregulating BNIP3 and MFN2 expression, thereby protecting mitochondria and cardiomyocyte nuclei. SND, SAC, and GBMA all alleviated mitochondrial functional impairment in the cardiomyopathy model. They could trigger energy metabolism reprogramming (reducing the expression of the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex subunits PDC-E2 and PDC-E3, and increasing the expression of OXPHOS-CI and OXPHOS-CIV) to optimize mitochondrial energy supply efficiency. SMC could downregulate CII expression in OXPHOS and exert some mitochondrial protective effects, but failed to significantly improve mitochondrial functional impairment. CONCLUSIONS: SND and SAC administration improve Dox-induced cardiomyopathy. They could protect mitochondria and cardiomyocyte nuclei through optimizing mitochondrial energy metabolism efficiency and inhibiting autophagy, while the specific active constituents and their absorption routes remain to be determined. This study elucidates the molecular mechanism by which the adminstration of SAC in SND improves Dox-induced cardiomyopathy, providing new scientific evidence for the combined clinical application of SND and Dox. It also offers a new approach to the research of the substance basis of TCM prescriptions, namely, focusing on the self-assembled substances present in the decoction, rather than assuming the active components are small molecules, to accurately reveal the overall effects of TCM prescriptions and the scientific connotation of their compatibility. It should be noted that the current findings are based on a single batch of SND, and further validation using multiple batches is required to confirm the consistency of the observed effects.

articles.title: Catalpol alleviates glandular and pulmonary injury in primary Sjögren's syndrome via regulation of sphingolipid metabolism.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: In traditional Chinese medicine, pSS-related oral and ocular dryness is associated with depletion of yin and body fluids, while pulmonary involvement may reflect impaired lung moistening. Rehmannia glutinosa is traditionally used to nourish yin, generate fluids, and relieve dryness. Catalpol, its major iridoid glycoside, may provide a pharmacological basis for these traditional uses. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study investigated the protective effects of catalpol in experimental pSS and examined the involvement of KDSR-mediated sphingolipid metabolism. MATERIALS AND METHODS: An antigen-induced experimental Sjögren's syndrome (ESS) mouse model, interferon-γ-stimulated A253 cells, and transforming growth factor-β-stimulated NIH-3T3 fibroblasts were used. Pseudo-targeted sphingolipidomics, multi-cohort transcriptomic analysis, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, cellular thermal shift assays, and KDSR knockdown were performed. RESULTS: Catalpol improved salivary secretion and reduced glandular inflammation and epithelial apoptosis in ESS mice. It also attenuated ESS-associated pulmonary inflammation and fibrosis-related changes and suppressed fibroblast activation. Integrated sphingolipidomic and transcriptomic analyses identified disease-associated KDSR upregulation and alterations in the sphinganine/3-ketodihydrosphingosine ratio. Molecular simulation and cellular thermal shift assays supported a potential interaction between catalpol and KDSR. Catalpol reduced KDSR expression and inhibited integrin/FAK/MYH9 signaling, whereas KDSR knockdown attenuated its protective effects in vitro. CONCLUSIONS: Catalpol ameliorated glandular dysfunction and pulmonary injury in experimental pSS. These effects were associated with KDSR-mediated sphingolipid metabolism and suppression of integrin/FAK/MYH9 signaling.

articles.title: Zhenwu Decoction improves myocardial energy metabolism and mitochondrial integrity in pressure overload-induced heart failure partly through AMP-activated protein kinase signaling.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Zhenwu Decoction (ZWD), recorded in the Shang Han Lun, is traditionally used for yang deficiency with fluid retention, a pattern relevant to congestion and impaired cardiac function. Its mitochondrial mechanism in pressure-overload heart failure remains unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: To evaluate the cardioprotective effects of ZWD and the contribution of AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK)-related signaling. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Male C57BL/6J mice subjected to transverse aortic constriction received low-, medium-, or high-dose ZWD (4.32, 8.64, or 17.28 g/kg/day, respectively) or the positive control captopril. Cardiac function, remodeling, oxidative stress, energy metabolites, mitochondrial ultrastructure, transcriptomics, and metabolomics were assessed. In angiotensin II-injured H9c2 cardiomyoblasts, small interfering RNA-mediated AMPK silencing was used to assess pathway dependence. RESULTS: ZWD improved systolic function and reduced ventricular dilation, injury biomarkers, collagen accumulation, and oxidative imbalance, with the most evident effects at the high dose. It increased adenosine triphosphate and acetyl-coenzyme A, reduced adenosine diphosphate and adenosine monophosphate, and preserved mitochondrial ultrastructure. These changes were accompanied by increased AMPK phosphorylation and sirtuin 1 abundance and reduced dynamin-related protein 1 phosphorylation. Multi-omics analyses identified treatment-associated changes in energy-related pathways. AMPK silencing attenuated, but did not completely abolish, the mitochondrial and metabolic effects of ZWD. CONCLUSIONS: ZWD ameliorated pressure-overload cardiac dysfunction and improved myocardial energy homeostasis and mitochondrial integrity. AMPK silencing partially attenuated the cellular response, supporting AMPK involvement in these protective effects, alongside increased sirtuin 1 abundance and reduced dynamin-related protein 1 phosphorylation.

articles.title: Polysorbate-based mixed micelles for protein stabilization: Development of manufacturing methods for phosphatidylcholine-polysorbate 80 systems and comparison to polysorbate 20 systems.
articles.abstract: Surfactants are commonly employed in protein formulations because proteins can undergo denaturation and particle formation. In the domain of pharmaceuticals, polysorbates (PS) such as PS20 and PS80 are extensively used as non-ionic surfactants in pharmaceutical formulations. However, polysorbates themselves may contribute to formulation instabilities, motivating efforts to reduce their concentration. In our recent work, the properties of mixed micelles of PS20 with a phospholipid as a stabilising excipient for protein formulations were characterised, in which part of the PS was substituted by a phospholipid. In this study, we examine the stability of mixed micelles of PS80 in the presence of hydrogenated soybean phosphatidylcholine, a potential protein-stabilising system. We first established and characterised a preparation protocol for PS80 mixed micelles. Subsequently, an evaluation was conducted of their protein-stabilising properties in shaking studies on a monoclonal antibody to assess colloidal stability under stress. Visual inspection and particle analysis were applied to monitor particle formation, and size-exclusion chromatography was used to monitor high molecular weight species. In the third step of the research, the stabilising properties of both PS80 and PS20 mixed micelle systems were assessed across the tested concentration range (0.004-0.4 mg·mL-1). This was accompanied by a direct comparison with the corresponding polysorbates. Transmission and dynamic light scattering indicated that mixed micelles were obtained at concentrations reaching 20 mg·mL-1 and phospholipid fractions around 50 %. In the context of shaking studies conducted on a monoclonal antibody, the presence of mixed micelles was found to be associated with a reduction in the formation of particles and high molecular weight species. The performance of the mixed micelles was found to be comparable to that of the polysorbates with respect to the endpoints measured under the conditions tested.

articles.title: Design and 99mTc-radiolabeling of an imidazopyridine-hydrazone hybrid: A promising tumor-targeted radiopharmaceutical.
articles.abstract: A novel imidazopyridine-hydrazone Schiff base ligand, N'-(2-hydroxybenzylidene)-2-(1H-imidazo[1,2-a]pyridin-3-yl)acetohydrazide (HIPAH), was synthesized, characterized, and evaluated as a potential tumor-imaging radiopharmaceutical. The ligand exhibited moderate antiproliferative activity against MCF-7, HepG2, and A549 cancer cell lines with IC50 values of 18.6 ± 1.2, 24.3 ± 1.5, and 32.8 ± 2.1 μM, respectively. Radiolabeling with technetium-99m was successfully achieved with a maximum radiochemical yield of 98.2 ± 0.6% under optimized conditions. The resulting 99mTc-HIPAH complex demonstrated excellent in vitro stability, retaining 96.8 ± 0.6% and 94.5 ± 0.9% radiochemical purity after 24 h in saline and serum, respectively. Molecular docking suggested a favorable interaction of the 99mTc-HIPAH complex within the VEGFR2 binding site, with a predicted binding affinity of -9.3 kcal/mol. Biodistribution studies in Ehrlich solid tumor-bearing mice showed progressive tumor uptake reaching 7.92 ± 0.33 %ID/g at 4 h post-injection, accompanied by rapid blood clearance and a maximum tumor-to-non-target ratio of 8.61. These findings support further investigation of 99mTc-HIPAH as a potential candidate for tumor imaging by SPECT.

articles.title: Early indicators of glass delamination in pharmaceutical borosilicate vials under alkaline stress conditions.
articles.abstract: Although borosilicate glass is widely regarded as chemically stable under neutral or mildly acidic conditions, its chemical durability may be compromised under alkaline conditions due to alkali-hydrogen ion exchange and hydrolytic dissolution of the silicate network, which are recognized precursors to glass delamination. This study investigates the delamination propensity and chemical resistance of Type I pharmaceutical glass vials with and without internal surface treatments after exposure to an alkaline model solution under accelerated aging conditions. Multimodal analytical techniques were employed to characterize glass-solution interactions. Inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES) was used to quantify leached elements (Si, B, Na, Al), while pH measurements monitored changes in the solution. Particle formation was assessed by scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and stereomicroscopy. SEM analysis revealed surface degradation features including pitting, lamellae formation, and silicate network dissolution. Uncoated vials (1 and 5) exhibited pronounced degradation, evidenced by elevated silicon concentrations, increased pH, and the formation of glass-derived particles. In contrast, interior-coated vials (2-4) preserved chemical and structural integrity, showing negligible surface damage and no detectable particle formation, even under alkaline stress conditions. These findings demonstrate that early degradation indicators, such as subvisible particle release and silica leaching, are sensitive markers of glass instability. Moreover, durable silicon-based coatings effectively mitigate delamination risk and significantly enhance the suitability of glass containers for alkaline or otherwise aggressive pharmaceutical solutions.

articles.title: CMKLR1 contributes to diurnal variation in brain injury after cardiac arrest by promoting lactate production in microglia.
articles.abstract: Previously, the results of our clinical study have suggested that circadian rhythm have an impact on neurological outcomes following cardiac arrest and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CA/CPR), but the underlying mechanisms remain unknown. Here, using a mouse model of CA/CPR, we aimed to unravel the underlying mechanisms of the diurnal variation in CA/CPR-induced brain injury. The mice received five minutes of CA either in the active phase or in the inactive phase. To identify novel therapeutic targets for the impact of circadian rhythm on CA/CPR-induced brain injury, we applied high throughput RNA-seq analysis to profile mRNAs with differentially expression in the hippocampus of the two groups. Since it has been reported that CMKLR1 is beneficial for inhibiting neuroinflammation and improving neurological outcomes among many neurological diseases, we centered on this gene and clarified that its main cellular source is microglia. The correlation between CMKLR1 expression in hippocampus and neurological outcomes after CA/CPR was elucidated by CMKLR1 activation and knockout in microglia. The impact of CMKLR1 on microglial function, especially glucose metabolism, was clarified using BV2 microglia cell line by glucose uptake analysis, seahorse analysis and carbon 13 tracing. As a result, CA/CPR happening at active phase leads to better neurological outcomes with upregulation of microglial CMKLR1 in the hippocampus of mice. Our findings suggest that elevated microglial CMKLR1 expression in the hippocampus contributes to improved neurological outcomes after CA/CPR by promoting lactate production in microglia.

articles.title: Trends and patterns of antipsychotic medication use during pregnancy: A population-based study.
articles.abstract: AIM: The prescription of antipsychotic medication during pregnancy, particularly second-generation antipsychotics, has increased in several countries in recent decades. This population-based study investigated trends and patterns in antipsychotic medication use during pregnancy between 2011 and 2023 in Northern Ireland (NI), UK. The purpose was to improve understanding about how these medicines are used during pregnancy, including patterns of antipsychotic discontinuation across pregnancy. METHODS: Data from the Northern Ireland Maternity System (NIMATS) were linked to dispensed prescribing data from the Enhanced Prescribing Database (EPD) and the NI Multiple Deprivation Measure 2017 (NIMDM). Overall temporal trends were identified, and subsequently stratified by subtype (first- and second-generation antipsychotics [FGAs and SGAs]). Usage was evaluated by pregnancy exposure period (12 weeks before pregnancy and by trimester). A separate analysis investigated patterns across trimesters in women who had been dispensed antipsychotics 12 weeks before pregnancy, including concomitant dispensing of antidepressants. RESULTS: The cohort included 287 757 singleton pregnancies in 175 938 women aged over 16 years, with an overall prevalence of antipsychotic use of 79.9 per 10 000 pregnancies. The prevalence of antipsychotic usage increased by 71% from 59 to 101 per 10 000 pregnancies between 2011 and 2023 (p = .001). SGA usage almost tripled from 32 to 93 per 10 000 pregnancies, whereas FGA usage decreased by 73% from 30 to 8 per 10 000 pregnancies in 2011 compared with 2023. Overall usage of antipsychotics decreased across trimesters. CONCLUSION: Overall antipsychotic prevalence during pregnancy increased over the study period, most notably SGA usage, whereas FGA usage decreased.

articles.title: Early-stage inhibition of HIV-1 subtypes A, B, and C gag- protease chimeras by Penicillium chrysogenum P03MB2 metabolites and activity against cell-to-cell spread.
articles.abstract: Despite the success of antiretroviral therapy, human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) cell-to-cell spread remains a major barrier to viral eradication. This study evaluated the antiviral activity of secondary metabolite fractions derived from Penicillium chrysogenum P03MB2 against cell-free HIV-1 infection of patient-derived Gag-protease chimeric viruses representing HIV-1 subtypes A, B, and C, and investigated its impact on cell-to-cell spread. Crude fungal extracts from oat-grown cultures were fractionated using mixed-mode cation exchange (MCX) solid-phase extraction. Cytotoxicity was assessed in TZM-bl cells by MTT assay, antiviral activity was evaluated using a luciferase reporter assay. In silico molecular docking explored predicted interactions between five identified metabolites, including Cytochalasin J, and entry-associated targets (CCR5, CXCR4, and gp120). Cell- to cell transmission was assessed using Jurkat co-culture assays and flow cytometry. The 45% MCX Oats fraction emerged as the most active candidate exhibiting low cytotoxicity (CC₅₀ > 300 µg/mL) and potent antiviral activity across all chimeric variants (IC₅₀: 0.221-1.007 µg/mL; Selectivity Indices: 271-1235). Time-of-addition analysis indicated that maximal inhibition during the early infection stages. Molecular docking identified favourable predicted binding compatibility for Cytochalasin J against CCR5 (reaching -10.9 kcal/mol), CXCR4, and gp120 targets, sharing predicted interacting residues with reference drugs. Furthermore, the fraction significantly reduces newly infected target cells in the cell-to-cell transmission model compared to untreated controls. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that 45% MCX Oats fraction exhibits potent antiviral activity against cross-clade antiviral activity against HIV-1 Gag-Pro chimeras and limits viral transmission in vitro, supporting further bioassay-guided isolation of its active constituents.

articles.title: Fourth-generation multi-costimulatory chimeric antigen receptor T cells targeting CD133 and integrin αvβ6 exert potent antitumor activity in cholangiocarcinoma.
articles.abstract: Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) is an aggressive and highly metastatic malignancy with limited responsiveness to conventional chemotherapy, underscoring the need for innovative therapeutic strategies. This study aimed to develop and evaluate fourth-generation chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells (CAR4; a multi-costimulatory CD28/4-1BB/CD27/CD3ζ design without a cytokine or other transgene payload) targeting CD133 and integrin αvβ6 to treat CCA. Two parallel CAR T-cell products, each incorporating a single antigen-recognition domain, were generated and evaluated independently rather than as one bispecific construct. We transduced activated human T lymphocytes with lentiviral constructs encoding anti-CD133 CAR4 and an integrin-targeted CAR (A20 CAR4), confirmed CAR expression by flow cytometry, then expanded them in vitro and evaluated therapeutic efficacy after intratumoral administration in a CCA xenograft nude mouse model. CAR4 T-cell treatment produced dose-dependent suppression of tumor growth and significant prolongation of survival compared with control and untreated groups. High-dose anti-CD133 and anti-integrin CAR4 T cells achieved greater tumor inhibition and numerically extended median survival beyond that observed with cisplatin. Histopathological analysis revealed no treatment-related abnormalities in heart, liver, spleen, or kidney tissues, and lung metastasis incidence was markedly reduced in high-dose CAR-treated groups. Quantitative real-time PCR analysis demonstrated coordinated downregulation of genes associated with angiogenesis (VEGF), matrix remodeling (MMP9), inflammatory signaling (COX-2, mPGES-1, TNF-α, IL-6), and immunosuppressive pathways (TGF-β, IL-10). These findings indicate that fourth-generation CAR T cells targeting CD133 and integrin αvβ6 exert potent antitumor activity in this model and that their activity is associated with transcript-level downregulation of tumor microenvironment-related genes, suggesting potential modulation of the tumor microenvironment that will require protein-level and functional confirmation. Antigen-dependent cytotoxicity was not directly assessed in vitro in the present study. Together, these data support further translational development of multi-costimulatory CAR T-cell platforms for CCA.

articles.title: Species differences in loxoprofen reductase activities: Roles of aldo-keto and carbonyl reductases in humans and rats.
articles.abstract: Loxoprofen is a widely used nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug designed as a prodrug to reduce gastrointestinal (GI) injury by hepatic biotransformation to its active form, trans-hydroxyloxoprofen. Preclinical studies in rats have suggested a relatively low incidence of GI injury with loxoprofen, whereas GI injury has been reported clinically. Although direct comparison between species is limited by differences in experimental and clinical conditions, species differences in loxoprofen metabolism may contribute to this discrepancy. We therefore compared the hepatic and intestinal metabolism of loxoprofen between humans and rats. In humans, the intrinsic clearance for trans-hydroxyloxoprofen formation was higher in the small intestine (16.3 mL/min per kg) than in the liver (10.5 mL/min per kg), whereas the opposite was observed in rats (2.5 vs 21.1 mL/min per kg, respectively). This human-specific intestinal metabolism was attributed to high expression of aldo-keto reductase (AKR) 1C3 and carbonyl reductase (CBR) 1. Recombinant rat Akr1c1, Akr1c14, and Cbr1 showed catalytic activity toward loxoprofen. Among them, Akr1c1 exhibited the highest activity and was expressed at higher levels in the liver than in the small intestine; however, it mainly produced inactive cis-hydroxyloxoprofen. Akr1c14 activity was insufficient to explain cytosolic activity in rat tissues, and Cbr1 expression was negligible in rat liver. Thus, enzymes other than Akr and Cbr families may be involved in loxoprofen metabolism in rat tissues. Overall, this study revealed a fundamental species difference in the reductive metabolism of loxoprofen, and the higher intestinal metabolic activity in humans may contribute to GI injury risk, although its clinical relevance requires further investigation. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: This study identifies a species difference in the reductive activation of the prodrug loxoprofen, demonstrating that humans exhibit higher intestinal than hepatic metabolic activity, whereas rats show the opposite pattern. The intestinal expression and contribution of AKR1C3 and CBR1 in humans further highlight species differences in loxoprofen metabolism that may influence exposure to the active metabolite. These findings underscore intestinal metabolism and species-specific enzyme expression in translational pharmacokinetics and safety.

articles.title: Misuse of obesity drugs exposes patients to serious and preventable harms: A French nationwide pharmacovigilance case series.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: The rapid uptake of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) for obesity has been accompanied by increasing use outside approved indications and medical supervision. Evidence regarding the harms associated with such misuse remains limited because these situations are not captured in clinical trials and are difficult to identify in healthcare databases. METHODS: A nationwide pharmacovigilance study was performed on adverse drug reactions (ADRs) involving a GLP-1 receptor agonist or GLP-1/GIP co-agonist used in a misuse context and reported to the French pharmacovigilance system between January 2021 and January 2026. Misuse included inappropriate use outside approved indications, dosing recommendations, contraindications or medical supervision requirements. RESULTS: Seventy-two cases were identified, 58% of which were serious. Patients were predominantly female (83%) and young (median age 30 years), with five cases involving minors. Gastrointestinal disorders accounted for 77.7% of reports. Serious ADRs included acute pancreatitis (n = 9), paralytic ileus, gastroparesis, ketoacidosis and severe hypoglycaemia. Among cases with available dosing information, overdosing was involved in 76.4%. In nearly two-thirds of cases, drugs were obtained outside any medical framework through relatives, social media, online sources or the black market. More than half of all cases were reported during the final year of the study period. DISCUSSION: Misuse of GLP-1 RAs is increasing and is associated with serious but largely preventable harm. Unsupervised access, excessive dosing and use of unregulated products appear to be the principal drivers of risk. These findings support stronger measures to limit inappropriate access and improve risk communication regarding GLP-1 therapies.

articles.title: Mechanistic insights into vincristine interactions with azoles and dasatinib: Implications for neurotoxicity in paediatric patients using physiologically based pharmacokinetic modelling.
articles.abstract: AIMS: This study aimed to investigate the mechanisms and pharmacokinetic consequences of vincristine (VCR) drug-drug interactions (DDIs) with azole antifungals and dasatinib (DAS). METHODS: In vitro enzyme and transporter assays were conducted to characterize VCR metabolism and inhibition by posaconazole (POS), voriconazole (VRZ), fluconazole (FLZ) and DAS. Paediatric physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) models were developed using in vitro parameters and further refined using empirical Bayesian estimates from a VCR population pharmacokinetic model. Cytotoxicity was assessed using dorsal root ganglion (DRG) cell assays. RESULTS: POS competitively inhibited CYP3A4 and CYP3A5 (Kᵢ = 1.62 and 1.35 μM) and P-gp (IC50 = 7.72 μM), whereas VRZ competitively inhibited CYP3A4 and CYP3A5 (Kᵢ = 8.87 and 4.22 μM) and additionally exhibited mechanism-based inhibition of CYP3A4 (KI = 16.24 μM, kinact = 0.0263 min-1). FLZ showed weak inhibition of CYP3A4 and CYP3A5 (Kᵢ > 60 μM), whereas DAS showed moderate inhibition (Kᵢ = 1.99-4.42 μM). The simulated VCR clearance was also approximately halved (CL = 0.59 vs. 0.33 L/h/kg) when co-administrated with POS. Moreover, PBPK modelling indicated that intravenous POS and VRZ increased VCR AUCs by more than twofold. In vitro DRG cell assays demonstrated a concentration-dependent potentiation of VCR-induced cytotoxicity by POS. CONCLUSIONS: Collectively, these PBPK model predictions suggest that POS and VRZ may represent high-risk perpetrators of VCR DDIs in children and may help guide future dose optimization and toxicity management, pending confirmation in prospective clinical studies.

articles.title: Thymoquinone suppresses papillary thyroid carcinoma by impairing autophagic flux via the PDZK1IP1/HMGCS1 axis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIM: Thymoquinone (TQ), the principal bioactive constituent of Nigella sativa, has antitumor activity in multiple malignancies, but its mechanism in papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) remains incompletely defined. EXPERIMENTAL PROCEDURE: We evaluated the effects of TQ on PTC cell proliferation, apoptosis, autophagic flux, and tumor growth, and examined the PDZK1IP1/HMGCS1 axis. KEY RESULTS: TQ reduced viability and clonogenic growth in TPC-1 and BCPAP cells, increased apoptosis, downregulated PCNA and Bcl-2, and upregulated cleaved caspase-3, cleaved PARP, and BAX. TQ also increased autophagy-related vesicles and p62 and LC3-II levels. Tandem mRFP-GFP-LC3B reporter imaging showed accumulation of both yellow dual-positive and red-only LC3 puncta. Together with pharmacological modulation using bafilomycin A1, chloroquine, and rapamycin, these findings supported impaired late-stage autophagic processing. Integrated public PTC datasets and TQ-treated TPC-1 RNA-seq data identified PDZK1IP1 as a candidate mediator. PDZK1IP1 knockdown enhanced, whereas overexpression attenuated, TQ-induced proliferation inhibition, apoptosis, and autophagy-marker accumulation. HMGCS1 was identified as a downstream effector; its overexpression partially rescued these effects in both TPC-1 and BCPAP cells. In xenografts, TQ suppressed tumor growth, reduced Ki67, PDZK1IP1, and HMGCS1, and increased LC3 and p62. CONCLUSION AND IMPLICATIONS: TQ suppresses PTC progression by impairing autophagic flux and downregulating PDZK1IP1/HMGCS1.

articles.title: Microcystin-LR exposure induces cartilage degeneration and dysregulates osteoarthritis-associated targets: an integrative computational and experimental study.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Microcystin-LR (MC-LR), a prevalent cyanotoxin in eutrophic freshwater, is becoming a more widespread environmental contaminant as global warming promotes cyanobacterial blooms, and its health effects may extend beyond its well-documented hepatotoxicity. METHODS: Here, we integrated network toxicology, machine learning, molecular dynamics simulation (MDS), and in vitro and in vivo experiments to investigate the role of MC-LR in osteoarthritis (OA). A total of 368 predicted MC-LR targets were intersected with OA-related differentially expressed genes from five batch-corrected Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) datasets. RESULTS: Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) identified a disease-correlated red module (r = 0.61, p = 2.3e-13), and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression narrowed the candidates to a six-gene diagnostic signature (FAP, IGF1R, IGF1, MMP9, CRABP2, and ITGA4), with a combined area under the curve (AUC) of 0.910. CIBERSORT analysis indicated altered macrophage polarization and T-cell redistribution within the osteoarthritic microenvironment. Molecular docking and 100-ns MDS showed that MC-LR formed thermodynamically favorable and stable complexes with the five upregulated core targets, with FAP exhibiting the strongest binding affinity (-10.3 kcal/mol). In human chondrocytes, MC-LR exposure was cytotoxic (IC50 = 13.09 μM) and upregulated the mRNA levels of CRABP2, FAP, IGF1, ITGA4, and MMP9, consistent with the in silico predictions. Intra-articular injection of MC-LR in mice induced dose-dependent knee cartilage degeneration, with matrix loss and elevated OARSI scores. DISCUSSION: Together, these findings associate MC-LR exposure with cartilage degeneration under experimental conditions and implicate PI3K-Akt signaling, focal adhesion, and extracellular matrix remodeling as candidate mechanisms, extending the recognized effects of cyanotoxins beyond the liver and highlighting chronic pollutant exposure as an underrecognized potential risk factor for degenerative joint disease.

articles.title: Hydroxychloroquine-induced cytotoxicity in ARPE-19 cells involves PI3K/AKT-associated signaling: network toxicology and functional validation.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hydroxychloroquine (HCQ) is widely used for the long-term treatment of autoimmune and rheumatologic disorders, but retinal toxicity remains an important adverse effect. Although lysosomal and autophagic dysfunction have been implicated in HCQ-associated retinal injury, the signaling networks involved in the cellular response to HCQ remain incompletely understood. This study investigated the potential involvement of PI3K/AKT-associated signaling in HCQ-induced cytotoxicity. METHODS: Network toxicology and molecular docking were integrated to identify candidate HCQ-associated targets, followed by experimental validation in human retinal pigment epithelial ARPE-19 cells. Cell viability was evaluated by CCK-8 assay, and apoptosis was assessed by Annexin V/PI flow cytometry. The expression of predicted hub genes and proteins was examined by qRT-PCR and Western blotting. AKT phosphorylation was evaluated across HCQ concentration and time gradients. The AKT activator SC79 was further used in pharmacological rescue experiments to assess the functional involvement of AKT signaling in HCQ-induced apoptosis. RESULTS: Network analysis identified PIK3CA, PIK3R1, SRC, JAK2, and PTPN11 as candidate hub proteins associated with PI3K/AKT-related signaling. Molecular docking suggested potential interactions between HCQ and these proteins, with variable docking energies among targets. HCQ reduced ARPE-19 cell viability in a concentration-dependent manner, with a 24-h IC50 of 59.51 μM, and increased apoptosis with increasing concentrations. qRT-PCR revealed concentration-dependent and gene-specific transcriptional responses rather than uniform suppression of all five hub genes, whereas Western blotting showed an overall reduction in the abundance of the candidate hub proteins after 24 h HCQ exposure. AKT phosphorylation exhibited dynamic regulation: short-term HCQ exposure increased p-AKT/AKT at higher concentrations, whereas an independent 30 μM time-course experiment showed an overall decline in AKT phosphorylation during prolonged exposure. Importantly, SC79 pretreatment enhanced p-AKT/AKT under HCQ exposure and partially attenuated HCQ-induced apoptosis. CONCLUSION: These findings support the involvement of PI3K/AKT-associated signaling in HCQ-induced cytotoxicity in ARPE-19 cells. HCQ induces concentration- and time-dependent alterations in this signaling network, while pharmacological enhancement of AKT signaling partially reduces the apoptotic response. The results provide functional evidence that AKT signaling contributes to the cellular response to HCQ and support further investigation of PI3K/AKT-associated signaling in HCQ-related RPE injury.

articles.title: Metabolite-GEN: integrated prediction of sites of metabolism, reaction class, and metabolite structures using graph edit networks.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Predicting the metabolic fate of drug candidates remains a central challenge in pharmaceutical research, with direct implications for efficacy, safety, and pharmacokinetic optimization. METHODS: We present Metabolite-GEN, an integrated graph neural network framework that predicts SOM and cytochrome P450-mediated reaction class from molecular graph representations, then uses these predictions to enumerate and rerank feasible metabolite structures. The framework was evaluated by five-fold scaffold-stratified cross-validation on 578 parent-metabolite pairs spanning 12 CYP-mediated reaction classes from the MetXBioDB database, followed by a single evaluation on a scaffold-disjoint held-out test set of 144 molecules. RESULTS: In cross-validation the model achieved mean SOM atom-ranking top-1/top-3/top-5 accuracies of 56.9% ± 6.7%, 78.6% ± 3.2% and 87.5% ± 1.8% (MRR 0.698), reaction class accuracy 37.2% ± 11.4% (weighted F1 0.365), and metabolite structure top-1/top-3/top-5 accuracies of 56.6% ± 4.1%, 73.4% ± 2.4% and 79.1% ± 3.7% (MRR 0.653). On the test set, SOM accuracies were 54.9%, 79.2% and 86.8% (MRR 0.688), reaction class accuracy 31.9% (weighted F1 0.323, macro F1 0.271), and metabolite structure accuracies 53.5%, 72.2% and 75.0% (MRR 0.626). DISCUSSION: The framework returns explicit metabolite structures rather than atom-level scores, and the candidate pool for a typical compound is short enough to inspect directly, so the output can be acted on without further filtering-prioritizing compounds for metabolic-stability screening, flagging reactive metabolite liabilities, and focusing experimental metabolite identification.

articles.title: Engineered Mycobacterium smegmatis-based intrapleural immunotherapy remodels the pleural immune microenvironment for malignant pleural effusion treatment.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Malignant pleural effusion (MPE) is a common and devastating complication of advanced malignancies, particularly lung cancer, with limited therapeutic options and poor prognosis. Immune checkpoint inhibitors and cytokine therapies have shown promise in solid tumors but are constrained by dose-dependent toxicity and limited efficacy in the pleural cavity. Engineered Mycobacterium smegmatis (M. smegmatis) co-expressing a PD-L1 inhibitor and interleukin-15 immunocytokine (Ms-PI15) represents a novel in situ vaccine platform capable of sustained local drug delivery with favorable biosafety profiles. Here, we investigated the therapeutic efficacy and underlying mechanisms of intrapleural Ms-PI15 administration in a murine MPE model. METHODS: A syngeneic MPE mouse model was established by intrapleural inoculation of luciferase-expressing Lewis lung carcinoma (LLC-Luc) cells into C57BL/6 mice. Mice were treated with intrapleural injections of PBS, Ms-vector (empty vector control), or Ms-PI15. Tumor burden was monitored by bioluminescence imaging. Pharmacokinetics and biodistribution of Ms-PI15 were evaluated using DIR fluorescence imaging and bacterial colony enumeration. Flow cytometry and immunohistochemistry were employed to characterize immune cell populations in the tumor microenvironment, spleen, and thoracic draining lymph nodes (TDLNs). Biosafety was assessed by histopathological examination and serum biochemistry. RESULTS: Intrapleural administration of Ms-PI15 significantly suppressed MPE development and pleural tumor growth compared with PBS and Ms-vector controls. DIR fluorescence imaging and CFU enumeration demonstrated that Ms-PI15 accumulated predominantly in the pleural tumor microenvironment and TDLNs, peaking at 72 h post-administration, with minimal dissemination to distant organs. Mechanistically, Ms-PI15 remodeled the immune microenvironment by promoting maturation of CD80+CD86+ myeloid dendritic cells (mDCs), driving M1 polarization of tumor-associated macrophages (increased CD86+, decreased CD206+), and significantly enhancing infiltration of CD8 T cells and NK1.1+ NK cells in the pleural tumor, spleen, and TDLNs. No significant histopathological abnormalities or serum biochemical alterations were observed in major organs following Ms-PI15 treatment, confirming its favorable biosafety profile. CONCLUSION: Intrapleural administration of the engineered M. smegmatis Ms-PI15 effectively inhibits MPE progression by remodeling the pleural immune microenvironment toward an antitumor phenotype, while maintaining excellent biosafety. These findings provide a preclinical foundation for the development of intracavitary bacterial immunotherapy as a novel treatment strategy for malignant pleural effusion.

articles.title: Apigenin promotes neuronal norepinephrine release via GPR30/PLCβ1-Ca2+-Syt1 signaling to enhance astrocytic lactate and exert neuroprotection in D-galactose-induced cognitive impairment.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: AD, a prevalent neurodegenerative disorder clinically defined by progressive cognitive impairment, is pathologically featured by early dysfunction of the locus coeruleus, depletion of noradrenergic (NE) neurons, and dysregulated astrocytic glycogen metabolism, which collectively compromise patients' daily functioning. Although Api, a common phytoestrogen, has shown therapeutic efficacy in diverse diseases, its role and mechanism in AD remain unexplored. METHODS: To address this gap, we evaluated the protective effects of Api against D-gal-induced cognitive deficits through behavioral and histomorphological assessments. Untargeted metabolomics was performed to profile metabolic alterations in the locus coeruleus (LC), complemented by targeted metabolomics focusing on specific pathways. Putative targets were predicted by molecular docking and verified via cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA), while molecular biology approaches were adopted to elucidate the underlying signaling cascades. RESULTS: Api significantly ameliorated D-gal-induced cognitive impairment and increased hippocampal NE and lactate levels with enhanced neuronal activity. Metabolomics indicated that Api regulates energy metabolism pathways including TCA cycle, amino acid metabolism, glycolysis/gluconeogenesis, and glutathione metabolism. Specifically, Api elevated NE and lactate in the LC. GPR30 was identified and validated as the key target via molecular docking and CETSA, showing strong binding affinity. Mechanistically, Api activates GPR30 on noradrenergic neurons to regulate PLCβ1-Ca2+-Syt1 signaling, promoting NE release, which in turn drives astrocytic glycogenolysis and lactate production, thereby relieving neuronal energy deficits. CONCLUSION: Collectively, this study not only clarifies the PLCβ1-Ca2+-Syt1-dependent mechanism of Api in aging-related cognitive impairment, but also highlights NE and lactate elevation as a promising therapeutic approach.

articles.title: Integrating whole-exome and genotyping array data for pharmacogenetic typing: a comparative evaluation with whole-genome sequencing in UK Biobank.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) provides comprehensive coverage of coding, non-coding, and rare variants for pharmacogenetic star-allele typing, but cost and computational demands limit its population-scale use. Whole-exome sequencing (WES) and imputed genotyping arrays are more widely available, yet their WGS-referenced performance remains incompletely defined. METHODS: We benchmarked star-allele calls from WES, imputed array data, and an integrated call set combining WES and array data against an Aldy-derived WGS analytical reference across 33 pharmacogenes in 1,450 multi-ancestry UK Biobank participants. We also developed PGxIntegrator, an open-source workflow that harmonizes WES and array data and enables scalable Aldy-based star-allele calling. RESULTS: Using WES or imputed array data alone, 25 of 33 genes reached high diplotype concordance with the WGS analytical reference (≥95%); the integrated call set also achieved ≥95% concordance for 25 genes and improved or maintained concordance relative to the better-performing single platform for 29 genes overall. The largest incremental gains among high-concordance loci were observed for CYP1A1, CYP3A4, and DPYD, where integration improved concordance by 1.3-3.3 percentage points over the better-performing single platform, consistent with complementary recovery of non-coding and rare haplotype-defining variants. In contrast, UGT1A1 and CYP2D6 remained challenging despite integration. DISCUSSION: For CYP2D6, the WGS analytical reference was generated by a single computational caller and was not orthogonally validated; concordance therefore reflects agreement with this reference rather than clinical typing accuracy. These findings provide practical gene-level guidance for population-scale pharmacogenetic analysis when WGS is unavailable.

articles.title: ROS-responsive GelMA/L-Arginine hydrogel with locally sustained NO release for accelerated skin wound healing.
articles.abstract: Nitric oxide (NO) plays crucial regulatory roles in accelerating cutaneous wound repair via modulating angiogenesis and macrophage polarization. Herein, a reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive GelMA/L-arginine (L-Arg) composite hydrogel was fabricated through 405-nm photocrosslinking for localized NO delivery and high-efficiency wound treatment. Physicochemical characterizations verified that L-Arg incorporation maintained the favorable moldability and interconnected porous microstructure of pristine GelMA hydrogel, and enabled sustained ROS-triggered NO release under oxidative microenvironment. In vivo full-thickness skin defect rat models demonstrated that the GelMA/L-Arg hydrogel markedly expedited wound closure, achieving a healing rate of 93.7% at day 14, and facilitated ordered re-epithelialization with a collagen area fraction of 64.6%. Further immunofluorescence results confirmed that the hydrogel improved regenerative quality by promoting mature angiogenesis with a vessel density of 116/mm2 and switching macrophages toward anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype. Systemic biosafety evaluation via major organ histological staining validated favorable biocompatibility without obvious organ toxicity. In conclusion, this multifunctional NO-releasing GelMA/L-Arg hydrogel represents a promising candidate for clinical wound dressing applications.

articles.title: Esculin and esculetin protect against bone loss in osteoporosis by rebalancing osteoblast and osteoclast functions.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Osteoporosis is characterized by uncoupled bone remodeling where resorption outpaces formation. This study investigated the roles of two natural coumarins, Esculin (ECL) and Esculetin (ECLT), in bone metabolism. METHODS: We evaluated the bidirectional effects of ECL and ECLT on primary osteoblasts and RAW264.7-derived osteoclasts in vitro. In vivo, the translational protective efficacy of the compounds was assessed using ovariectomized (OVX) and sciatic nerve transection (DEN) mouse models, representing postmenopausal and disuse osteoporosis, respectively. Evaluations included serum biochemical analysis, histological staining, micro-computed tomography (Micro-CT), and three-point bending biomechanical tests. RESULTS: In vitro assays identified optimal pharmacological concentrations of 50 μM for ECL and 10 μM for ECLT, with both compounds dose-dependently promoting osteoblast proliferation and mineralization while simultaneously inducing osteoclast apoptosis and downregulating key resorptive genes. Co-administration of ECL and ECLT demonstrated enhanced efficacy, greater than either monotherapy in several key readouts. In both OVX and DEN in vivo models, the combinatorial regimen markedly ameliorated systemic inflammation and oxidative stress, and successfully rebalanced circulating bone turnover markers. Furthermore, the dual therapy robustly prevented the deterioration of three-dimensional trabecular and cortical bone microarchitecture and substantially improved the functional biomechanical strength of the femurs. CONCLUSION: The concurrent application of ECL and ECLT protects against bone loss by concurrently promoting osteoblast function and suppressing osteoclast formation, representing a promising bidirectional strategy for osteoporosis management.

articles.title: Olanzapine induces Mdivi-1-resistant disruption of insulin signaling in skeletal muscle cells.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Second-generation antipsychotics such as olanzapine (OLZ) are widely prescribed because they produce fewer extrapyramidal adverse effects than first-generation agents. However, OLZ is strongly associated with metabolic dysfunction, and alterations in mitochondrial dynamics have been proposed to contribute to these effects. We investigated whether OLZ-induced mitochondrial dysfunction is linked to impaired insulin signaling in skeletal muscle cells and explored a potential interaction with the mitochondrial fission regulator dynamin-related protein 1 (DRP1). METHODS: L6 skeletal myoblasts were treated with OLZ, alone or in combination with the mitochondrial fission inhibitor Mdivi-1. Insulin signaling, glucose uptake, mitochondrial morphology, and insulin-stimulated mitochondrial bioenergetics were evaluated. In parallel, molecular dynamics simulations and MM/PBSA calculations were performed using a common DRP1/Mg2 + receptor model to compare the interactions of protonated OLZ and Mdivi-1 within the DRP1 GTPase domain. RESULTS: OLZ reduced insulin-mediated signaling and glucose uptake, promoted mitochondrial fragmentation, and impaired the insulin-induced increase in mitochondrial bioenergetic activity. Co-treatment with Mdivi-1 partially rescued OLZ-induced mitochondrial fragmentation but did not restore insulin responsiveness. Molecular simulations showed that protonated OLZ and Mdivi-1 remained within the same hydrophobic region of the DRP1 GTPase domain and shared an anchoring interaction involving Ile252. Their calculated MM/PBSA interaction free energies were similar (-22.26 ± 1.7 and -24.50 ± 0.5 kcal mol- 1, respectively), supporting compatible occupancy of a shared binding region but not demonstrating high-affinity or GTP-competitive binding. DISCUSSION: These findings indicate that OLZ disrupts mitochondrial dynamics and bioenergetics while decreasing insulin sensitivity in skeletal muscle cells. However, the dissociation between recovery of mitochondrial morphology and persistence of insulin resistance suggests that excessive mitochondrial fission alone does not account for OLZ-induced metabolic dysfunction. The computational results are compatible with an interaction of OLZ with the DRP1 GTPase domain but do not establish DRP1 as its primary pharmacological target. OLZ-associated insulin resistance therefore likely involves additional, potentially extramitochondrial mechanisms.

articles.title: Estimating metabolic pathway overlap in precision oncology: integrating pharmacogenetics and polypharmacy.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: While metabolic pathway overlap is frequent in polypharmacy patients, the modification of genotype-predicted metabolic phenotypes by other substrates is not well established yet, and its relevance for pharmacogenetic implementation in gastrointestinal oncology has not been systematically assessed. We aimed to quantify the overlap between pharmacogenetically relevant treatment pathways and concomitant medications in routine gastrointestinal cancer care. METHODS: Guideline-recommended drugs for gastrointestinal malignancies were evaluated regarding their dependence on pharmacogenetically relevant enzymes. In parallel, real-world co-medication profiles were analyzed to assess the prevalence of inhibitors and inducers of these identified enzymes, as well as the substrate-mediated pathway sharing. RESULTS: Only a minority of systemic anticancer drugs recommended in treatment guidelines were directly affected by established pharmacogenetic polymorphisms, mainly involving CYP2D6, CYP2C19, CYP2C9, and related pathways. In contrast, co-medication profiles with medications sharing common metabolic pathways were highly prevalent whereas recognized moderate or strong inhibitors were much less frequent (<10%). CONCLUSION: Although relatively few anticancer therapies are directly affected by actionable pharmacogenetic variants, the potential for metabolic pathway overlap may increase the clinical relevance of pharmacogenetics in gastrointestinal oncology. By systematically quantifying the coexistence of inhibiting co-medication as well as substrate-mediated pathway sharing, this study provides descriptive explorative estimates of the metabolic pathway-overlap burden. These findings suggest that pharmacogenetic implementation strategies should consider both genotype and medication-related pathway overlap to better inform estimates of drug exposure and support precision oncology.

articles.title: Population pharmacokinetics and model-informed precision dosing of busulfan in Chinese pediatric allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation: a prospective real-world cohort study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Busulfan is a cornerstone of conditioning regimens for pediatric allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), yet its narrow therapeutic index and high pharmacokinetic variability necessitate individualized dosing. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a population pharmacokinetic (PopPK) model for busulfan in Chinese pediatric allogeneic HSCT recipients, characterize the exposure-response relationship, and establish a model-informed precision dosing (MIPD) strategy for clinical implementation. METHODS: This prospective, single-center study was conducted at Children's Hospital of Fudan University between August 2020 and January 2026. Plasma busulfan concentrations were quantified using a validated HPLC-MS/MS. PopPK analysis was performed using nonlinear mixed-effects modeling. The association between busulfan exposure (AUC0-6h) and clinical outcomes was evaluated using logistic regression. Monte Carlo simulations were performed to derive an age- and body weight-stratified dosing regimen, and a closed-loop MIPD workflow was developed for clinical implementation. RESULTS: A total of 290 pediatric HSCT recipients contributed 1543 busulfan concentration measurements. A two-compartment model with first-order elimination adequately characterized busulfan pharmacokinetics. Body weight and age were significant determinants of clearance. For a 70 kg reference individual, the population estimates of clearance and central volume of distribution were 12.4 L/h and 40.8 L, respectively. The model demonstrated good predictive performance in internal evaluation. Under empirical dosing, only 47.6% of patients achieved the target AUC0-6h of 900-1350 μM min/L. Busulfan exposure (AUC0-6h) was not significantly associated with mortality (OR, 1.002; 95% CI, 1.000-1.004; P = 0.069) or acute graft-versus-host disease (OR, 1.001; 95% CI, 1.000-1.002; P = 0.161). Monte Carlo simulations supported an age- and body weight-stratified initial dosing regimen. A closed-loop MIPD workflow was established in which the initial dose is selected according to the simulated dosing regimen, followed by therapeutic drug monitoring and pharmacist-physician collaborative dose adjustment when AUC0-6h falls outside the prespecified target range. CONCLUSION: A PopPK model with body weight and age as key determinants of busulfan clearance was developed and evaluated in a large real-world cohort of Chinese pediatric allogeneic HSCT recipients. The proposed MIPD framework provides a practical approach for optimizing busulfan therapy in this population.

articles.title: Therapeutic potential of hydroxybenzoic acid and lentinan in mitigating glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis: an experimental study.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: The present study aimed to elucidate the therapeutic efficacy and mechanistic roles of Hydroxybenzoic Acid and Lentinan in counteracting glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis (GIOP) in mice, with a focus on bone metabolism, inflammation, and oxidative stress pathways. METHODS: Sixty-eight male Swiss Albino mice were randomly assigned to seven groups: Healthy Control, Osteoporosis (methylprednisolone 10 mg/kg), Teriparatide (3 μg/kg), Low-Dose Lentinan (200 mg/kg), High-Dose Lentinan (400 mg/kg), Low-Dose HBA (50 μg/kg), and High-Dose HBA (100 μg/kg). In the study, all treatments were administered daily for a duration of 10 weeks. RESULTS AND DISCUSSION: Methylprednisolone administration resulted in marked deterioration of bone quality, with significant reductions in 25(OH)D3, IGF-1, and increased osteocalcin, TNF-α, IL-1β, HSP-27, RANK, and RANKL expression, accompanied by severe trabecular bone loss, all treatment groups showed notable recovery, with the most pronounced restoration in teriparatide and high-dose hydroxybenzoic acid groups. Mechanistically, hydroxybenzoic acid exerted potent anti-osteoclastic effects through RANK/RANKL pathway suppression, while Lentinan enhanced osteoblastic activity and mitigated inflammatory damage. In conclusion, these results provide preclinical evidence that HBA and lentinan warrant further investigation as potential adjuncts to established anti-osteoporotic therapy in the setting of long-term glucocorticoid use.

articles.title: Liraglutide regulate osteogenesis-resorption via macrophage under compressive stress.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Joint diseases always caused by mechanical pressure induced-inflammation and bone resorption. With advancing age, joint wear-and-tear intensifies while reparative capacity diminishes. Liraglutide is a common medication used to lower blood sugar and improve blood lipids, and it is widely used in elderly patients. This study investigated whether liraglutide (Lira) regulates macrophage-mediated bone metabolism under mechanical pressure and elucidated the molecular mechanisms. METHODS: RAW264.7 macrophages were exposed to varying pressures (1-3 g/cm2) via custom-weighted glass coverslips. Cell viability was assessed by CCK-8 and Live/Dead staining. Cells were pretreated with 250 nmol/L Lira, and the expression of osteoclast-related (Piezo1, NFATc1, TRAP) and inflammation-related (TNF-α, iNOS, IL-1β, TRAF6, NF-κB/p-NF-κB) molecules was detected by qRT-PCR, immunofluorescence, and Western blotting. Conditioned media from treated macrophages were used to culture MC3T3-E1 pre-osteoblasts, and osteogenic markers (BMP2, RUNX2, ALP, OCN) were evaluated. RESULTS: Pressure at 2 g/cm2 for 4 h optimally induced osteoclastogenesis and inflammation. Lira did not affect Piezo1 expression but significantly suppressed NFATc1 and TRAP at both mRNA and protein levels. Lira also inhibited the TRAF6-NF-κB pathway, reducing TNF-α, iNOS, and IL-1β expression. Conditioned media from Lira-treated macrophages significantly upregulated BMP2, RUNX2, ALP, and OCN in MC3T3-E1 cells, indicating indirect promotion of osteogenesis. CONCLUSION: Liraglutide reverses pressure-induced bone metabolic imbalance through a triple mechanism: inhibiting osteoclastogenesis, attenuating inflammation, and indirectly promoting osteogenesis via macrophage modulation. This study provides the first evidence of liraglutide's molecular network in regulating bone metabolism under mechanical stress, supporting its therapeutic potential in pressure-related degenerative joint diseases such as osteoarthritis and temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis.

articles.title: Time-dependent pharmacokinetic changes and renal SGLT2 expression alterations of dapagliflozin under high-altitude hypoxia in diabetic rats.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study investigated the time-dependent effects of high-altitude hypoxia on the pharmacokinetics (PK), renal sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) expression, and glycemic response to dapagliflozin in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) rats. METHODS: T2DM was induced in male Wistar rats via high-fat diet and low-dose streptozotocin. In the acute study, rats received a single oral dose of dapagliflozin (1 mg/kg) after a 3-day exposure to normoxia or simulated 6000 m hypoxia. In the chronic study, rats received daily dapagliflozin (1 mg/kg) during a 14-day period under normoxia or chronic hypoxia. Plasma dapagliflozin concentrations were determined by UPLC-MS/MS. Fasting blood glucose was monitored serially, and renal cortical SGLT2 protein levels were quantified by ELISA at study endpoint. Individual exposure-response relationships were assessed by Spearman correlation. RESULTS: Acute hypoxia caused a dramatic PK perturbation: AUC0-t and Cmax increased by 6.58-fold and 5.06-fold, respectively, compared with acute normoxia (all p < 0.01). Chronic hypoxia produced a significant but attenuated effect: AUC0-t and Cmax increased by 2.11-fold and 1.69-fold, respectively (all p < 0.01), representing an approximately 70% reduction in the magnitude of PK change under chronic versus acute exposure. Chronic hypoxia was also associated with significantly attenuated early glycemic reduction at days 4 and 7 (p < 0.01), though fasting blood glucose levels converged by day 14. Although these observations were temporally associated, a direct causal link is not supported, as SGLT2 was measured only at day 14 whereas glycemic differences emerged earlier (days 4-7). Pooled analysis showed no significant correlation between dapagliflozin exposure and day-14 fasting blood glucose, whereas group-stratified analysis revealed a significant negative correlation between AUC0-t and day-14 fasting blood glucose in normoxic rats only. CONCLUSION: Dapagliflozin pharmacokinetics undergo time-dependent adaptation under high-altitude hypoxia. Exposure-response analysis suggested a hypoxia-induced dissociation between dapagliflozin exposure and glycemic response. These findings underscore the need for dedicated clinical PK-PD monitoring in high-altitude populations and provide a descriptive framework for future mechanistic and translational investigations.

articles.title: In vivo blood and ex vivo brain solid-phase microextraction coupled with LC-MS/MS for mapping unbound cannabidiol, phase I metabolites, and endocannabinoid tone.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Evaluating the central nervous system distribution of cannabidiol (CBD) and its dynamic interplay with the endocannabinoid system (ECS) is fundamentally constrained by conventional tissue homogenization, which fails to distinguish pharmacologically active fractions from total pool of analyte. To resolve active biophase kinetics, this study established a minimally invasive solid-phase microextraction (SPME) coupled with LC-MS/MS platform to monitor CBD, its phase I metabolites, and key endocannabinoids directly within circulating blood in vivo and intact anatomical brain regions ex vivo. METHODS: Male rats received a single oral dose of medicinal cannabis (100 mg/kg CBD). Systemic fractions of analytes were captured via in vivo SPME (10-min sampling window) in the circulating blood of living animals. Following sacrifice, ex vivo SPME (30-min sampling window) was deployed across four anatomical brain regions (hippocampus, amygdala, cerebellum, and brainstem). SPME-based microextraction was performed across a 1-6 h temporal baseline, and was then cross-validated against traditional solid-liquid extraction (SLE). Analytes were quantified using validated, high-sensitivity liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) method. RESULTS AND DISCUSSION: In vivo blood sampling captured rapid oral absorption of parent CBD, reaching a maximum free systemic concentration (Cmax ≈160 μg/mL) at 2 h post-dose followed by rapid systemic clearance. Among the phase I metabolites, only 6-hydroxy-CBD (6-OH-CBD) was recovered from circulating blood at the 2-h interval at trace levels. Mean systemic 2-arachidonoylglycerol (2-AG) concentrations were higher than baseline at all post-dose time points, with the highest mean value observed at 6 h. Ex vivo brain microextraction uncovered marked neuropharmacokinetic heterogeneity. Furthermore, while total tissue SLE detected abundant phase I metabolites with total 7-OH-CBD higher than parent CBD, SPME may reflect limited freely available concentrations and/or strong tissue association of those analytes in brain structures. This exploratory study confirms the technical feasibility of coupling living intravascular extractions with localized regional brain sampling of CBD and endocannabinoids. By demonstrating that CBD concentrations clear dynamically and account for only a minute fraction of total tissue homogenate mass, this methodology-driven proof of concept establishes a more accurate bioanalytical framework for evaluating novel ECS modulators and lipophilic neuropharmacological candidates.

articles.title: Enhancing student confidence and preparedness in pharmacology: a virtual pre-laboratory approach.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Laboratory practicals are a core component of undergraduate pharmacology education but are often associated with student anxiety due to lack of familiarity with the lab environment and experimental procedures. Virtual pre-laboratory activities have the potential to address this challenge by allowing students to familiarise themselves with the practical setting and procedures in advance of in-person classes. METHODS: A virtual, interactive desktop-based pre-laboratory resource (VR-Lab) was developed to support second year BSc Medical Pharmacology students undertaking in-vitro organ bath experiments. The VR-lab incorporated a 360-degree laboratory environment, stepwise procedural guidance and formative activities. A mixed-methods evaluation was conducted with a cohort of 34 students using Likert-scale survey responses and open-ended feedback following the first practical session. Comparisons of summative assessment performance were made with a previous cohort without access to the VR-Lab. RESULTS: Students reported high levels of engagement, usability and perceived educational value. All respondents reported the VR-lab enhanced preparedness for and confidence during the in-person laboratory session. Qualitative feedback highlighted the importance of procedural familiarisation, stepwise guidance, and embedded multimedia content in supporting engagement. Feedback also identified areas for improvement included navigation and accessibility on smaller devices. No significant difference in summative assessment performance was observed between cohorts. CONCLUSION: Virtual pre-laboratory resources may enhance the student experience of practical pharmacology teaching by reducing barriers associated with unfamiliar environments, supporting confidence and engagement without directly influencing assessment outcomes.

articles.title: Dichloroacetate attenuates experimental acute liver injury and reduces hepatocyte apoptosis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute liver injury (ALI) is a severe clinical condition characterized by rapid hepatic dysfunction and may progress to acute liver failure. Hepatocyte apoptosis is a critical pathological event in ALI. Dichloroacetate (DCA), an inhibitor of pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase, has been reported to regulate cellular metabolism and apoptosis; however, its role in ALI remains unclear. This study investigated the protective effects and potential mechanisms of DCA in experimental ALI. METHODS: DCA was evaluated in mouse models of ALI induced by lipopolysaccharide (LPS)/d-galactosamine (D-GalN) or tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α)/D-GalN. Liver injury and hepatocyte apoptosis were assessed by serum transaminase activities, histopathology, and TUNEL staining. Hepatic immune cell profiles were analyzed by flow cytometry. Hepatic cytokine mRNA expression and serum cytokine levels were measured by RT-qPCR and ELISA, respectively. Apoptosis-related proteins were examined by Western blotting. Additional acetaminophen (APAP) and thioacetamide (TAA) models were used to assess DCA-mediated hepatoprotection. RESULTS: DCA pretreatment substantially attenuated LPS/D-GalN-induced ALI, as evidenced by reduced serum transaminase levels, less severe histopathological injury, and decreased hepatocyte apoptosis. This hepatoprotective effect was not accompanied by significant changes in surface TLR4 abundance on Kupffer cells, serum inflammatory cytokine levels, or hepatic immune cell composition at the examined time points. Notably, DCA treatment was associated with reduced cleaved caspase-3 expression and increased A20 protein levels in both LPS/D-GalN- and TNF-α/D-GalN-treated mice. CONCLUSION: DCA attenuates experimental ALI and is associated with reduced hepatocyte apoptosis and increased A20 expression.

articles.title: Network pharmacology-based investigation of the therapeutic effects and molecular mechanisms of oxymatrine in psoriasis.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Psoriasis is a common chronic inflammatory skin disease with complex pathogenesis, and current therapeutic agents have certain limitations. Oxymatrine (OMT), the primary active component of the traditional Chinese herb *Sophora flavescens*, possesses multiple pharmacological effects including anti-inflammation and anti-proliferation, but its molecular mechanism against psoriasis remains incompletely elucidated. This study systematically dissected the "component-target-pathway" regulatory network of OMT against psoriasis using a network pharmacology approach to predict its underlying mechanisms, which were further validated via clinical specimen analysis and in vitro cell experiments. METHODS: OMT targets were collected from the Traditional Chinese Medicine Systems Pharmacology (TCMSP) database and literature mining, while psoriasis-related targets were obtained from 5 databases including GeneCards. After target mapping, drug-core target and protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks were constructed, and core targets including EGFR, AKT1, JAK2, and BCL2 were identified. Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses, molecular docking, and 100 ns molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were conducted. Clinical validation was carried out in patients receiving 8 weeks of OMT treatment. HaCaT keratinocytes were divided into control, M5 cytokine cocktail-induced model, methotrexate (MTX) positive control, and OMT intervention groups for in vitro experiments. RESULTS: Enrichment analyses revealed significant enrichment in inflammatory response regulation, apoptotic signaling, and multiple JAK/STAT-related pathways. OMT exhibited favorable binding affinities to core targets such as EGFR, JAK1, JAK2, and STAT3.
