Notably, OMT-JAK1 and OMT-STAT3 complexes demonstrated excellent thermodynamic stability as validated by MD simulations. Clinically, patients' **Psoriasis Area and Severity Index (PASI)** scores were significantly reduced, lesion histopathology was markedly improved, and aberrant EGFR-JAK/STAT and apoptosis-related molecule expression was significantly reversed. In vitro, OMT significantly inhibited M5-induced EGFR-JAK/STAT phosphorylation and activation, and restored apoptotic balance. DISCUSSION: These findings suggest that OMT exerts therapeutic effects against psoriasis by inhibiting EGFR phosphorylation, upregulating SOCS1, thereby suppressing excessive JAK/STAT signaling activation, modulating apoptosis-related protein expression, and ultimately promoting keratinocyte apoptosis while inhibiting their proliferation and inflammatory responses. This study provides experimental evidence for the clinical application of OMT in psoriasis treatment.

articles.title: Tacrolimus ameliorates pulmonary hypertension associated with pulmonary fibrosis via modulation of vascular remodeling.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is frequently complicated by pulmonary hypertension (IPF-PH), a severe condition that worsens symptoms, reduces exercise capacity, and shortens survival. Current anti-fibrotic and PH-targeted therapies show limited efficacy in IPF-PH, and the therapeutic role of tacrolimus in this composite disease remains underexplored. METHODS: A bleomycin-induced IPF-PH rat model was established. Rats were randomized into control, bleomycin model, treprostinil (positive control), and tacrolimus (0.05 mg/kg/day, subcutaneous, 21 days) groups. Right ventricular systolic pressure (RVSP), echocardiography, right ventricular and lung histology, immunohistochemistry, qRT-PCR, and Western blot were assessed. In vitro, C166 endothelial cells and primary rat pulmonary arterial endothelial cells were stimulated with bleomycin with or without tacrolimus; MOVAS smooth muscle cells were stimulated with TGF-β1 with or without tacrolimus. Endpoints included cell viability, tube formation, ROS, SOD/GSH, apoptosis, proliferation/migration, and MAPK/PI3K/AKT signaling. RESULTS: Tacrolimus reduced RVSP, improved PAT/PET and right heart function, attenuated right ventricular hypertrophy and pulmonary fibrosis, and decreased vascular wall thickness and α-SMA expression. It also downregulated fibrosis markers Fn1 and Col1a1. In endothelial cells, tacrolimus restored P-VEGFR2/VEGFR2 and VE-cadherin expression, promoted tube formation, reduced apoptosis (Bax/Bcl-2, cleaved caspase-9/3), and alleviated oxidative stress (ROS, SOD/GSH, Keap1/HO-1). In smooth muscle cells, tacrolimus inhibited TGF-β1-induced proliferation and migration and reduced Ki67 expression. Mechanistically, tacrolimus suppressed MAPK (JNK, ERK, p38) and PI3K/AKT pathway activation in vivo and in vitro. DISCUSSION: Tacrolimus ameliorates bleomycin-induced IPF-PH through vascular remodeling-oriented, multi-target effects, including endothelial protection, suppression of oxidative stress and apoptosis, and inhibition of smooth muscle proliferation, partly via MAPK and PI3K/AKT signaling. These findings support tacrolimus as a potential therapeutic candidate for IPF-PH, especially in patients with prominent vascular remodeling, while highlighting the need for further dose-response, target-specific, immunomodulatory, and delivery optimization studies before clinical translation.

articles.title: Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase at the crossroads of redox homeostasis and regulated cell death in erythrocytes.
articles.abstract: Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) provides the sole source of NADPH in mature erythrocytes, fueling the cell's essential antioxidant defenses. Although G6PD deficiency is traditionally tied to acute oxidative hemolysis, red cell loss extends beyond simple membrane rupture. This perspective evaluates G6PD-dependent NADPH supply as a metabolic redox checkpoint that controls the balance between erythrocyte survival, regulated cell death, and clearance. Reduced NADPH availability can limit glutathione regeneration and thus decrease GPX4-dependent lipid peroxide detoxification. Although this biochemical relationship provides a possible link between redox imbalance and erythrocyte injury, the direct involvement of ferroptosis and necroptosis-like pathways in mature erythrocytes remains insufficiently proven. Acute hemolysis, in this view, is a downstream consequence of these regulated events rather than the primary cause. G6PD is essential for erythrocyte survival as their sole source of NADPH. G6PD deficiency alone does not always cause cell death, but under oxidative stress, it acts as a metabolic checkpoint that shifts red blood cells from survival to regulated death rather than simple osmotic lysis.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics and prognosis of liver injury in patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitor-based therapy: a real-world retrospective study.
articles.abstract: AIMS: This study aimed to examine the clinical characteristics, injury patterns and 6-month recovery of liver injury in patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitor -based therapy. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study of patients receiving ICIs at Tianjin Union Medical Center (The First Affiliated Hospital of Nankai University) between January 2020 and June 2024, with follow-up censored December 2024 and a minimum 6 months. We analysed the clinical characteristics, severity, dynamic changes in liver function, and recovery factors of patients with ICI-based therapy-related liver injury (ICI-LI). RESULTS: Of 682 patients, 83 (12.17%) developed ICI-LI (cholestatic 73.49%, mixed 20.48%, hepatocellular 6.02%). Among 83 patients, baseline alkaline phosphatase (ALP), gamma-glutamyl transferase, and total bilirubin, and peak alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) trend to be higher with greater liver injury severity. The rate of change in liver function parameters differed by subtype: hepatocellular injury showed rapid ALT/AST increases, cholestatic injury a marked but slower ALP increase, and mixed injury features of both. In univariate analysis, age, peak ALT, and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) > 3 were associated with poor 6-month recovery (P < 0.05); in multivariate analysis, only NLR >3 remained associated (OR = 10.917, 95% CI 1.552-76.817, P = 0.016). ROC analysis yielded AUCs of 0.702 for continuous NLR (cut-off 2.955, rounded to 3) and 0.694 for NLR >3. CONCLUSION: Cholestatic injury was the predominant subtype with PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor-containing therapy. Changes in liver function parameters varied according to the clinical pattern. NLR >3 warrants further investigation as a potential exploratory biomarker for poor recovery in ICI-LI.

articles.title: Substitutability of cocaine and social interaction in male and female rats before and after intermittent access cocaine self-administration.
articles.abstract: RATIONAL AND OBJECTIVES: Previous studies have found that cocaine and social interaction act as substitutes in male rats, but it is unknown whether they are also substitutes in female rats. The two purposes of the present study were to compare male and female rats on the way cocaine and social reinforcement economically interact and to determine whether exposure to intermittent access (IntA) cocaine self-administration changes the interaction. METHODS: In a first phase, male (n = 16) and female (n = 17) rats were allowed to choose between cocaine and social reinforcement available at varying prices to determine how these reinforcers economically interact. Then, half of the rats of each sex received 12 sessions of IntA cocaine self-administration while the other half served as no-cocaine homecage controls. In a final phase, the way that cocaine and social reinforcement interacted was redetermined. RESULTS: Cocaine and social reinforcement were partial substitutes in male rats, replicating previous findings. In contrast, these reinforcers were not substitutes in females, but instead were independent economic goods. During IntA cocaine self-administration, female rats escalated their intake over sessions, but males did not. IntA cocaine exposure had no impact on reinforcer interactions. CONCLUSIONS: The sex difference in the way that cocaine and social reinforcement interacted suggests that one or both of these reinforcers may serve different functions in male and female rats. The results of this study contribute to growing research on the way that the broader behavioral economic context contributes to choice between drug and non-drug alternatives.

articles.title: Effects of chronic restraint stress on behavioral responses to haloperidol in rats treated with modafinil or methylphenidate.
articles.abstract: Chronic stress can alter behavior and neurobiological systems involved in cognition and psychostimulant responses. Modafinil (MOD) and methylphenidate (MPH) affect locomotor activity and cognitive performance, but how chronic restraint stress modifies subsequent behavioral responses to dopamine receptor blockade remains incompletely understood. This study evaluated behavioral responses to a haloperidol (HALO) challenge in restrained and unrestrained rats following chronic MOD or MPH treatment. Adult male Sprague-Dawley rats were allocated to two independent cohorts (MOD and MPH), each comprising 48 animals. Rats received daily oral MOD (75 mg/kg/day) or MPH (10 mg/kg/day) for 35 days, with or without restraint stress (2 h/day). Animals subsequently received a challenge dose of HALO (1​mg/kg, intraperitoneally) or saline. Locomotor activity was assessed in the home cage and open field, passive-avoidance performance was assessed using the Passive Avoidance Test, and head-dip frequency was recorded using the head-dip test. Data were analyzed separately for the MOD and MPH cohorts using three-way factorial ANOVA. HALO significantly reduced locomotor activity, passive-avoidance latency, and head-dip frequency, with the magnitude of these changes varying according to stress and chronic treatment conditions. Restraint stress increased open-field locomotion and reduced passive-avoidance latency and head-dip frequency in saline-treated animals. Chronic MOD and MPH treatment increased locomotor activity and head-dip frequency and increased passive-avoidance latency under saline-challenge conditions. However, reductions in passive-avoidance latency and head-dip frequency following HALO challenge cannot be attributed exclusively to memory-related or exploratory changes as catalepsy was not directly assessed and HALO-induced motor impairment may have contributed. These findings demonstrate stress- and treatment-dependent differences in behavioral responses to HALO following chronic psychostimulant exposure. Altered dopaminergic responsiveness is a possible interpretation, but the underlying neurochemical mechanisms remain to be established.

articles.title: Semi-Solid Extrusion 3D Printing of Dispersible Oral Dosage Forms: A Mini-Review of Disintegration Determinants.
articles.abstract: Semi-solid extrusion (SSE) three-dimensional printing (3DP) has become one of the most versatile additive-manufacturing routes for on-demand, personalized oral medicines. Because it processes hydrated polymeric inks at or near room temperature, SSE 3DP is especially attractive for dispersible dosage forms intended for pediatric, geriatric and dysphagic patients. Yet the mechanisms governing the disintegration of SSE-printed forms remain poorly defined and cannot be extrapolated directly from conventionally compressed dispersible tablets, whose cohesion arises from mechanical compaction rather than from a solvent-mediated, hydrogen-bonded network. This mini-review maps the literature published between 2015 and 2025 and critically analyses the manufacturing, formulation and structural-design factors that influence dispersibility. Across the corpus, disintegration is governed primarily by two controllable levers, The formulation composition and the post-printing processing, which together shape the dried polymer network. On this basis, three complementary and non-exclusive disintegration mechanisms are proposed: capillary penetration through the printed micro-architecture, swelling, and erosion or dissolution at interlayer interfaces. Most published formulations still reproduce conventional tablet geometries, thereby under-using the design freedom of 3DP, and quantitative structure-disintegration relationships remain scarce. These gaps define clear priorities for the rational design of the next generation of dispersible SSE-printed medicines.

articles.title: Comparing the Effectiveness of a Longitudinal Model With Logistic Regression for Binary Endpoints to Support Better Clinical Decision Making.
articles.abstract: Exposure-Response (ER) analyses are key to optimizing dosing regimens for the safe and effective use of drugs. The choice of modeling approach should depend on the questions being asked and on the method's ability to appropriately characterize the ER relationship. While logistic regression (LR) is a common choice to evaluate ER relationships for binary endpoints, limitations can affect its reliability. Specifically, it cannot explicitly account for time-varying exposure, necessitating the use of summary exposure metrics that may bias its results. Longitudinal models can address some time-dependent factors known to affect LR analyses, but these require greater resource investment. As a result, clearer guidance is needed for selecting appropriate exposure metrics in LR and for determining when the additional complexities of longitudinal models are warranted. In this study, we compared Markov modeling with LR using systematically varied simulations designed to evaluate multiple strengths of the ER relationship, representative pharmacokinetics for small and large molecules, early and late event onset, high and low dose modification rates, different total sample sizes, and multiple exposure metrics. Overall, Markov modeling demonstrated a superior ability to identify ER relationships, especially those of intermediate strength and in smaller sample sizes, and tended to yield less biased estimates of the drug effect. Results did not suggest advantages of event-based metrics for LR. This study is the first to demonstrate the effectiveness of a longitudinal model relative to LR for ER analyses, and it introduces a simulation framework that guides method and exposure metric selection across common drug development scenarios.

articles.title: Hepatic Erbin loss promotes CCl4-induced liver fibrosis by potentiating the TGF-β/Smad signaling in hepatocytes.
articles.abstract: Hepatocytes comprise the bulk of the organ parenchyma and are vulnerable to various kinds of insults. As a consequence, the injured hepatocytes trigger the progression of liver fibrosis by releasing the profibrotic factors. However, the exact mechanisms involved in the fate regulation of hepatocytes during liver fibrogenesis remain far from clear. Erbin is a cytoplasmic protein that is widely expressed in the epithelial cells at a wide range of tissues. In the present study, we found that Erbin was markedly decreased in hepatocytes in the murine models of CCl4-induced liver fibrosis, as well as in the biopsies of liver cirrhosis patients. Ectopic expression of Erbin protected the mice from CCl4-induced hepatocellular injury and liver fibrosis, whereas knockdown of Erbin aggravated the severity of CCl4-induced liver injury and fibrosis in mice. The mechanistic study showed that overexpression of Erbin suppressed the potential of TGF-β/Smad signaling in hepatocytes by hindering the nuclear translocation of pSmad2. In contrast, inhibiting Erbin potentiated TGF-β/Smad signal transduction. Finally, the pathological significance of Erbin in liver fibrosis was associated with its protective effects against the concomitant apoptosis of hepatocytes in the progression of liver fibrosis. In summary, our observations identify an important regulatory mechanism of TGF-β/Smad signaling in hepatocytes during the progression of liver fibrosis, and, thus, suggest a potential strategy for therapeutic intervention.

articles.title: Technetium-99m-labeled HBsAg-conjugated anionic linear-globular dendrimers: radiolabeling and preclinical biodistribution.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Radiolabeling of nanocarriers can facilitate preclinical evaluation of their biodistribution and organ accumulation in healthy mice. OBJECTIVES: HBsAg was conjugated to G2-ALGD using carbodiimide chemistry and subsequently radiolabeled with technetium-99m (D-HBsAg-⁹⁹ᵐTc). The resulting nanoplatform was characterized in terms of its physicochemical properties, radiochemical purity, and preliminary cytocompatibility. Its in vivo biodistribution was evaluated in BALB/c mice using single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) imaging and ex vivo radiometry. RESULTS: D-HBsAg-⁹⁹ᵐTc nanotracers were 148.3 ± 24.5 nm in size and showed a zeta potential of + 3.65 mV. FTIR verified amide bond formation at 1649 cm⁻¹ between the dendrimer's carboxyl groups and HBsAg's amino groups. They showed no significant cytotoxicity in HFF-2 cells up to 100 µg/mL after 24 h. These nanoconjugates achieved a radiochemical purity of 95.83% and remained radiochemically stable for 24 h without detectable technetium leakage. Ex vivo biodistribution and SPECT imaging demonstrated significantly greater hepatic accumulation of D-HBsAg-⁹⁹ᵐTc than free ⁹⁹ᵐTc (22.89 ± 0.45 vs. 0.88 ± 0.42%ID/g, P < 0.05). Compared with HBsAg-⁹⁹ᵐTc, D-HBsAg-⁹⁹ᵐTc exhibited comparable liver uptake (22.89 ± 0.45 vs. 20.78 ± 4.23%ID/g) but substantially lower splenic (6.34 ± 0.21 vs. 11.66 ± 0.28%ID/g) and gastrointestinal accumulation, indicating improved hepatic accumulation and reduced off-target distribution. CONCLUSION: This nanoplatform represents a promising technetium-99m-labeled nano-tracer and demonstrated preferential hepatic accumulation in healthy mice, supporting its feasibility for preclinical biodistribution studies. Future studies should evaluate its immunogenicity and antiviral activity in appropriate HBV animal models to determine whether it may have applications beyond preclinical biodistribution imaging.

articles.title: Human Airway Epithelial Cell Line Responses to Cigarette Smoke Extract and LPS: Insights Into Mucus and Cytokine Regulation.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Airway epithelial cells produce mucus to protect themselves against toxic agents and pathogens. However, excessive mucus accumulation, as seen in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), contributes to airway obstruction, inflammation, and reduced efficacy of inhaled therapies. OBJECTIVES: The aim of the study was to develop an in vitro model for evaluating cytokine production and mucus secretion in human airway epithelial cell lines, with potential application for drug screening. METHODS: Three human airway epithelial cell lines (A549, Calu-3, and NCI-H292) were stimulated for 24 h with cigarette smoke extract (CSE), alone or combined with lipopolysaccharide (LPS). In parallel, NCI-H292 and Calu-3 cells were co-cultured under the same conditions. MUC5AC, CXCL8/IL-8, CXCL1/GRO-α, and CCL2/MCP-1 expression was assessed by RT-qPCR, and protein secretion by ELISA. MUC5AC production in NCI-H292 was further evaluated by immunohistochemistry. RESULTS: In Calu-3 cells, stimulation had no significant effect on mucin or cytokine expression. In A549 cells, CSE + LPS induced a marked release of CXCL8/IL-8, CXCL1/GRO-α, and CCL2/MCP-1, but no mucus production. In NCI-H292 cells, LPS alone increased mucus production, and CSE + LPS had an additive effect on both mucins and cytokines (except CCL2/MCP-1). In NCI-H292/Calu-3 co-cultures, CSE + LPS enhanced MUC5AC gene expression, whereas LPS alone increased CXCL8/IL-8 secretion. CONCLUSION: Among the tested cell lines, NCI-H292 displayed the most consistent dual response in terms of mucus and cytokine production. This supports its use as a practical in vitro model for preliminary screening of therapies targeting airway inflammation and mucus hypersecretion.

articles.title: Real-World Comparative Effectiveness and Safety of Prasugrel Versus Ticagrelor After Acute Coronary Syndrome and Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.
articles.abstract: STUDY OBJECTIVE: To compare the real-world effectiveness and safety of prasugrel versus ticagrelor among patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in the United States. DESIGN: Retrospective new-user cohort study. DATA SOURCE: MarketScan Research Databases, 2017-2023. PATIENTS: Patients aged 18 years or older with ACS and PCI initiated on either prasugrel or ticagrelor were identified using International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM) diagnosis codes and prescription records. The prescription fill date was assigned as the index date. Patients were required to have continuous enrollment in their health care plan for 1 year prior to and including the index date. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Stabilized inverse probability treatment weighting was applied to balance baseline characteristics between treatment groups. Cox proportional hazards models with adherence adjustment were used to estimate 1 year risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE, composite of myocardial infarction [MI], ischemic stroke, or stent thrombosis), bleeding events, and individual MACE components. The study included 6662 prasugrel-treated and 25,452 ticagrelor-treated patients. Prasugrel was associated with a lower risk of MACE (3.83 vs. 5.61 events per 100 person-years; adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 0.72, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.65-0.92) and MI (3.43 vs. 4.73 events per 100 person-years; aHR 0.80, 95% CI 0.66-0.97) compared with ticagrelor, respectively. Bleeding risk did not differ between prasugrel versus ticagrelor (2.85 vs. 3.89 events per 100 person-years, respectively; aHR 0.92, 95% CI 0.74-1.13). Sensitivity analyses restricted to patients with high medication adherence and without contraindications to prasugrel showed similar results. CONCLUSION: Among commercially insured US patients with ACS undergoing PCI, prasugrel was associated with a lower risk of ischemic cardiovascular events compared with ticagrelor, without an increase in bleeding risk, including in patients with high medication adherence. These findings provide contemporary real-world evidence supporting the preferential use of prasugrel over ticagrelor following ACS and PCI in appropriately selected patients.

articles.title: Model-Derived Iopamidol Clearance and Creatinine-Based Kidney Function Estimates After Trauma: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: STUDY OBJECTIVE: To determine whether iopamidol administered during clinically indicated contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CE-CT) and measured in remnant serum can provide an individualized surrogate value for measured glomerular filtration rate (mGFR) after trauma to compare against creatinine-based estimates. DESIGN: Single-center retrospective observational cohort. SETTING: Academic medical center. PATIENTS: Seventy-six adults evaluated for trauma who underwent iopamidol-enhanced CT and had at least one quantifiable postcontrast concentration and serum creatinine measurement. INTERVENTION: None. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Population parameters of a previously developed two-compartment structural model were re-estimated using the study data and stochastic approximation expectation-maximization, followed by participant-specific conditional-mode clearance estimation. Individual iopamidol clearance was interpreted as mGFR (mGFRIOP). Agreement with Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance and nonindexed Chronic Kidney Disease Epidemiology Collaboration (CKD-EPI) creatinine estimated GFR was assessed; 449 serum creatinine measurements were modeled over 7 days. Median mGFRIOP was 99 mL/min (interquartile range, 59-125). Each 30-mL/min higher mGFRIOP was associated with a 0.11-mg/dL lower serum creatinine at iopamidol administration (95% confidence interval, 0.06-0.16; p < 0.001). Predicted serum creatinine values converged over 7 days despite differences in mGFRIOP (interaction p < 0.001). Estimates were within 30% of mGFRIOP in 71% of patients for CKD-EPI versus 59% for Cockcroft-Gault (p = 0.035). CKD-EPI had narrower 95% limits of agreement compared with Cockcroft-Gault (-73 to 57 vs. -82 to 74 mL/min, respectively) but increasingly underestimated higher mGFRIOP (proportional-bias p < 0.001). CONCLUSION: Cohort-specific iopamidol clearance estimates as a surrogate for mGFR can be generated from routine CE-CT and remnant serum samples that differ from creatinine-based estimates. Prospective validation against conventional mGFR is required before clinical use.

articles.title: Resistin is a new player in murine hippocampal neuronal cells: expression and action on cell metabolic activity, proliferation, cell cycle, and expression of selected proliferative and apoptosis genes in HT-22 cells.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Resistin, initially identified as an adipocyte-derived hormone, is associated with obesity, insulin resistance, and diabetes. However, its role in hippocampal neuronal cells remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the effects of resistin on neuronal hippocampal cell function. METHODS: Expression of Retn and its receptors (Ror1, Cap1, and Tlr4) was analysed in mouse hippocampal HT-22 cells using RT-qPCR. The effects of resistin (0.1, 1, and 10 ng/ml) on metabolic activity (alamarBlue), proliferation (BrdU), cell cycle distribution and apoptosis (Annexin V/PI flow cytometry) were evaluated. Expression of apoptosis- (Bax, Bcl2, caspases-3, -8, -9, and p53) and proliferation-related markers (cyclins A2, B1, D1, and E1) was assessed using RT-qPCR and Western blotting. Activation of ERK1/2 pathway and the involvement of ERK1/2 and TLR4 signalling in resistin action were examined using pharmacological inhibitors. RESULTS: HT-22 cells expressed resistin and all three investigated receptors. Resistin decreased cellular metabolic activity at 7 h but increased it at 24 h. It stimulated cell proliferation at both time points and altered the cell cycle distribution after 24 h. At a 1 ng/ml, resistin reduced Ccne1 transcript levels and modulated the levels of cyclins and apoptosis-related markers examined. Moreover, resistin decreased the Bax/Bcl2 ratio at both the mRNA and protein levels after 24 h as well as increased ERK1/2 phosphorylation at 5 h. Pharmacological inhibition of ERK1/2 pathway indicated the involvement of ERK1/2 signalling in the resistin-mediated regulation of metabolic activity and proliferation, while TLR4 signalling was involved in the regulation of Casp3 expression and cell proliferation in HT-22 cells. CONCLUSION: Resistin may act as a novel regulator of hippocampal neuronal cell function.

articles.title: Paralleled Polymer Degradation and Oxybutynin Release from Short-Chain Polyesters for In-Situ Forming Intravesical Implant Design.
articles.abstract: In situ forming implants (ISFI) for intravesical drug delivery represent a promising alternative to current treatment options for neurogenic detrusor overactivity (NDO). Previous formulations demonstrated opportunities for further optimization regarding the temporal alignment between drug release and polymer degradation, which may influence depot persistence during repeated administration. Therefore, different polyester grades with various molecular weights and solvent systems were investigated in order to parallel drug release and polymer degradation. Reducing the molecular weight from 38 to 2 kDa increased degradation threefold (from 8 to 25% within 72 h). Nevertheless, ISFI with PLGA 2 k were characterized by a high initial drug release of 20% after 24 h. By an increase of application frequency from once every nine days to every third day, the initial drug release was reduced to 10% within the first three days paralleling drug release and polymer degradation (10% after 72 h), resulting in a nearly linear relationship between these processes. These findings demonstrate that dose-splitting can effectively modulate release kinetics, supporting improved temporal alignment of drug release and polymer degradation without substantially increasing burst release. In addition, with a low molecular weight polyester grade, depot persistence may be further reduced under repeated administration conditions. Still, an ISFI administered every three days can distinctly improve the quality of life for NDO patients currently administering up to five doses daily.

articles.title: Scalable Workflow for Extracellular Vesicle Isolation, Purification and Storage Guided by Subtype-Specific Features.
articles.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EV) are promising drug delivery platforms; however, clinical translation is limited by challenges in scalable production and storage. This study evaluates how isolation, purification, and preservation strategies influence the physicochemical properties, yield, surface composition, and functional cargo of large EV (lEV) and small EV (sEV), using erythropoietin (EPO) as a model therapeutic cargo. EV were isolated by ultracentrifugation (UC) alone or combined with tangential flow filtration (TFF), and stored under - 80°C (reference condition), refrigerated, or lyophilized using a standard (Std Lyo) or a proprietary optimized cycle (Opt Lyo) designed to minimize structural damage without lyoprotectants. Refrigeration reduced particle recovery and altered surface charge in both EV subtypes, indicating decreased stability. Std Lyo induced structural alterations and fragmentation, particularly in sEV, only partially mitigated by trehalose addition. In contrast, Opt Lyo better preserved size distribution and physicochemical stability across subtypes. Both lyophilization cycles altered surface marker detectability, reflecting membrane reorganization. TFF markedly enhanced yield and purity, especially in sEV, but also modified EV composition and their response to Opt Lyo, influencing downstream stability. EPO cargo in lEV showed no significant differences across conditions, with lower mean values after lyophilization, whereas sEV were more sensitive. Uptake assays revealed subtype- and process-dependent differences in cellular internalization, with limited involvement of heparin-sensitive pathways under the tested conditions. Collectively, these findings support a scalable workflow in which TFF-based purification followed by UC and Opt Lyo maximize overall performance, while revealing subtype-specific vulnerabilities that define the final EV product and inform tailored optimization.

articles.title: Eutectic Mixture as a Novel Approach to Improve Compression Properties of Metformin Hydrochloride.
articles.abstract: Metformin hydrochloride (MET), an antidiabetic medication, possesses poor compression properties and severe elastic recovery, hindering its formulation via direct compaction. This study engineered MET eutectic mixture and cocrystals using freeze-drying and evaluated them for overcoming these compression liabilities and minimizing punch sticking propensity. Niacinamide (NI), a flexible carboxamide micronutrient beneficial in diabetes management, was evaluated alongside D-Mannitol (MAN), a brittle polyol benchmark excipient, at 1:1 and 1:2 molar ratios. Solid-state characterization (PXRD, FTIR, DSC and TGA) confirmed that both adjuvants yield a eutectic mixture at a 1:1 ratio and a distinct cocrystal phase at a 1:2 ratio. Morphologically, the MET-NI systems exhibited unique layered microstructures. Mechanical profile assessment showed that MET-NI eutectic mixture and cocrystals drastically improved MET plasticity, showing significantly reduced yield pressure via Heckel analysis compared to their corresponding physical mixtures. Consequently, the MET-NI systems displayed enhanced compactibility and tabletability, producing mechanically stable tablets at high drug-coformer loadings (99.5% w/w). Conversely, the MET-MAN formulations exhibited dominant brittle deformation, resulting in severe tablet lamination and capping at compaction pressures exceeding 150 MPa. Furthermore, punch sticking assessment revealed that the enhanced internal tablet strength (API:coformer - API:coformer bonding interaction) of MET-NI eutectics and cocrystals reduced punch sticking mass up to 10-fold compared to the physical mixture. This work demonstrates that particle engineering, particularly utilizing eutectic mixture approach via freeze-drying with flexible carboxamides like niacinamide, presents a highly viable approach for modifying the micromechanical properties of problematic drugs to facilitate seamless large-scale direct compaction manufacturing.

articles.title: Practical and Device-Independent Assessment of Spatial and Contrast Resolution in X-ray CT.
articles.abstract: Despite the increasing use of quantitative X-ray computed tomography (XRCT) analysis in pharmaceutical research, practical and device-independent approaches for objectively assessing image quality and defining acquisition conditions remain limited. As image quality in industrial XRCT is largely governed by spatial and contrast resolution, reliable evaluation of these parameters is essential. In this study, a systematic approach was developed for assessing these parameters in XRCT systems commonly used in pharmaceutical research. Most pharmaceutical materials exhibit low X-ray attenuation and limited intrinsic contrast, making reliable assessment of contrast resolution particularly important for quantitative image analysis. Readily available polymer monofilaments and light metal rods were used to evaluate spatial resolution by the 10-90% distance and contrast resolution by the contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR). The 10-90% distance was strongly dependent on CNR and converged to approximately 4-6 times the nominal pixel size with increasing CNR, regardless of imaging system, acquisition conditions, and sample material. Stable and robust spatial resolution measurements required a CNR of approximately 4 or greater. A separation index describing histogram peak separation was highly correlated with CNR (r = 0.9998) across all experimental conditions. Because CNR was proportional to the square root of effective exposure, the proposed approach enabled prediction of the acquisition conditions to achieve a target image quality level. This approach provides a practical and device-independent framework for image quality assessment and optimization of quantitative XRCT measurements.
